#4139. Feature: What Sony Live Service PS5 Games Are Still Alive?

All the cancelled projects and those that remain

Video games are cancelled internally all the time, but never in PlayStation's personal history have those cancellations had to happen in such a public manner. The current PS5 generation has seen the platform holder try to win the live service space, and a few years later, it's having to cancel most of the projects it revealed in attempting to achieve that.

To try and get a piece of the Fortnite pie, Sony made a hard and deliberate push into the Games as a Service space at the start of the PS5 generation. It acquired Destiny 2 studio Bungie to have it help the manufacturer do so, and at the height of the initiative, PlayStation planned to launch 12 live service games in just a few years.

The latest victim is Fairgames from Haven Studio, a developer set up to create the heist co-op title. It was announced in 2023, and three and a half years later, it's now been cancelled after failing to impress in a new round of private tests.

Times have changed, and company executives are finally learning you can't set out with the intention of making the next Genshin Impact or Apex Legends; it has to happen more naturally. Sony has learnt that the hard way, with many graves dug for its failed projects.

But what's still left of the push and remains in active development at PlayStation?

I'm going to document all the live service PS5 games from Sony that have been cancelled, released, and are still set to come (for now).

Here are all the PS5 games and projects Sony publicly announced or acknowledged that have now been cancelled:

Here are all the PS5 games Sony released that are considered live service:

Here are all the live service PS5 games Sony still has in the works:

By my count, that's nine game cancellations for projects Sony either confirmed or commented on publicly, six titles that have actually released, and four more that are currently in development. The disaster that was Concord means it can basically be discounted from the released list, despite the fact it did actually come out.

Then, the list of PS5 live service games currently in development could lose another title as soon as next month.

Horizon Hunters Gathering is currently being reworked into a more traditional co-op title, but if it doesn't impress in an evaluation planned for December, then it's getting cancelled too.

News PlayStation Scaling Back Horizon Live Service PS5 Game as Sony Failures Continue

Guerrilla has until December to impress Sony execs

Despite the consistent failure in the space, with only one big win to its name in the form of Helldivers 2, Sony has stated it's going to persist with live service titles. Back in June, boss Hideaki Nishino said the game model "attracts users on a global level".

He continued: "The genre itself is relatively new, and I think many people are trying various things, so we also want to continue to take on challenges within that context."

From Sony's perspective, those live service games aren't going anywhere despite the track record and industry shifts.

@RoomWithaMoose CoD, Fighting games, sports games and well most other games with a multiplayer element are live service games.

The first game ever released (Space Wars) was a multiplayer only shooter and multiplayer games have been consistently popular throughout the 48 years I have been gaming. Whether the game is Pong, Ice Hockey, Minecraft, Double Dragon, NARC, Wii Sports, Madden, Mario Kart, Street Fighter, Gauntlet, Ikari Warriors, Excitebike Minecraft, Diablo, Gran Turismo, Overcooked or Marvel Rivals lots of people enjoy playing with or against other people.

While there are a segment of gamers who have decided they hate playing with others and are deeply, personally offended by the existence of multiplayer games there is little evidence of such a hard dividing line or hard feelings among game developers (From Software and for that matter it’s partner Nintendo can do anything it wants and right now it is working on a PvEvP game though admittedly said game seems to be having teething troubles) or most of the game community.

While multiplayer games have an even higher fail rate than single player games (honestly investors looking for safe, steady returns should stay far away from gaming) success can be massive and long lasting so it always has been and always will be a temptation for developers and publishers.

While a portion of the internet gets wrapped up in behind the scenes stuff and boycotts and what have you most gamers focus on the games they want to play (be they multiplayer or single player, first or third party) so I don’t think Sony’s live service push has hurt it any (in no small part because MS’s purchase of Activision didn’t result in Activision becoming Bethesda).

Its worth remembering that at the end of the day Sony is a listed company, it exists solely for the benefit of it shareholders. Their willingness to invest is basically driven by revenue and profit (and growth of those). A spreadsheet somewhere tells Sony that even 2 moderate successes out of 14 attempts is worth it - and until the spreadsheet says differently they'll keep doing it. Business isn't about love and passion and joy - its simply about the spreadsheet I'm afraid.

#4138. Microsoft Announces Last-Minute Restock Of The Xbox Series X25 Console

Available at launch through the Microsoft Store and participating retailers

As we mentioned in our original version of this article, Xbox's tweet made it unclear whether the drop would happen on November 11th going into November 12th, or November 12th going into November 13th.

A bunch of people set their watches for "midnight local time" last night, and nothing ended up happening. Therefore, the new belief is that the drop will happen at midnight on the evening of November 12th.

This also appears to have been confirmed on the official Xbox website.

If you're keen for one of these, best of luck! Hopefully you manage to grab one.

Original Story: Ever since the Xbox Series X25 console first became available for pre-order in August, it's become hard to get your hands on one. The "Limited Edition" system quickly sold out, and became a target for scalpers within 24 hours as well.

If you were hoping to add the Series X25 to your collection (or the accompanying controller, for that matter), you might still have a chance - Microsoft says that a "limited" restock will be available on November 12th to mark the launch.

This apparently goes live at "midnight local time", which we assume means November 11th going into November 12th (although the tweet doesn't make this fully clear):

As you can see, the restock will be available on the official Microsoft Store / Xbox Store, but also at other participating retailers that have yet to be named. We assume most of them will be the ones that carried the original pre-order.

You can feel free to go back to our pre-order guide for the Xbox Series X25 console if you want easy to access to various links and pricing info, but just be aware that things might be a bit different for this restock, so it's worth searching around at midnight local time if the Microsoft Store version sells out quickly.

Are you hoping to get your hands on one of these? Let us know down in the comments section below!

Guide The Xbox Series X25 Is Now Available To Pre-Order, And Here's Where You Can Buy It

Following a brief early access period for lucky fans yesterday

#4137. Cosy Train Sim 'Station To Station' Arrives On Switch 2 Later This Month

Do you like trains? Of course you do, who doesn't like trains. Stupid question. Anyway, you're in luck, dear reader. The cosy train sim Station to Station is making its way to the Switch 2, launching on 26th November 2026.

Boasting lovely voxel visuals, Station to Station starts you off with a handful of rural structures, tasking you with creating stations and connections to expand your world and transform it into a lush, thriving landscape.

While it's ultimately a relaxing experience, you can also earn high scores by engaging with more strategic gameplay, allowing you to stack bonuses and multiply your income.

On Switch 2, you can expect to find mouse controls along with the game's Creative Mode, letting you explore community designs and share your own. The main game will contain 54 levels set across 7 regions.

Over on Steam, Station to Station currently commands a total of 1,248 user reviews, of which 89% are positive. It's also earned solid scores from critics too, including 8/10 from IGN and 4/5 from Tech Radar.

Mini Review Locomoto (Switch) - On The Right Cosy Track, But Has A Few Train Faults

#4136. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

And, as ever, it’s worth checking if you’re missing any of these Love and Deepspace codes to get some in-game freebies.

#4135. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

"Mass effect 2 was not perfect, but it benefited so much from setting realistic achievable goals"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

AAA development cycles have increased dramatically since Mass Effect 2 launched in 2010, to the point that it's not uncommon to see 10-year gaps between mainline releases i.e. The Elder Scrolls 6, GTA 6, and Fallout 5. Contrast that with the 26 months in-between Mass Effect 1 and 2, and you start to wonder what type of coffee the folks at now-defunct BioWare were drinking back then. The truth is, the size and scope of big-budget games have ballooned alongside development cycles, but the Mass Effect 2 team benefited from a number of other factors that seem sorely lacking in today's AAA landscape, as pointed out by Mass Effect 2 lead designer Christina Norman.

In a new tweet, Norman explains "how mass effect 2 came together in 18 months successfully," and well, it reads like a list of things AAA studios aren't doing anymore. First of all, "it was the same team that shipped mass effect," says Norman, adding that, "teams often have a lot of turn over," but for ME2, "the core team stayed the same." A novel concept, I know, but maybe there is something to the idea of maintaining a long-term vision and trusting your staff through highs and lows that results in long-term success.

Norman also says the team at BioWare "knew the timeline up front" and learned from Mass Effect 1 on a couple of points. "A lot of mistakes" were made developing Mass Effect 1 in Unreal, and so the developers "came into mass effect 2 knowing how to build" in that engine. Also, the Mass Effect 2 team was "ruthless about limiting scope," says Norman. "Mass Effect 1 was a much higher scope game and we had to cut about half of it just to ship. The team hated that and it was wasteful because a lot of work didn't ship. We cut our scope to the bone early on so no work was wasted."

How mass effect 2 came together in 18 months successfully: - It was the same team that shipped mass effect. Teams often have a lot of turn over, the core team stayed on for mass effect 2. - We knew the timeline up front (I believe the dragon age 2 team had their schedule pulled in six months or more which was rough( - We struggled a lot shipping mass effect 1 on unreal and we made a lot of mistakes. We came into mass effect 2 knowing how to build with unreal. - We were ruthless about limiting scope. Mass Effect 1 was a much higher scope game and we had to cut about half of it just to ship. The team hated that and it was wasteful because a lot of work didn't ship. We cut our scope to the bone early on so no work was wasted. - We listened to the player feedback on mass effect 1 and used that to decide what to cut, what to keep, and what to improve. Mass effect 2 was not perfect, but it benefited so much from setting realistic achievable goals given the short development timeline.November 8, 2026

Finally, and this sounds pretty key, BioWare "listened to the player feedback on mass effect 1 and used that to decide what to cut, what to keep, and what to improve. Mass effect 2 was not perfect, but it benefited so much from setting realistic achievable goals given the short development timeline."

Of course, Mass Effect 2 is considered by many to be the best game in the series, although there's definitely not a clear consensus on that in the community. The fact that it was made by the same team as the first game in just 18 months is staggering, and it's a somber reminder of the glory days in the wake of EA's cancelation of Mass Effect 5 and shutdown of BioWare.

#4133. GTA 6 Gets Its First Unboxing Video As Shipping Begins For Xbox & PS5

Here's a look at what's inside the physical edition

While Rockstar Games mentioned a date of November 12th for shipping the physical edition of GTA 6 for Xbox and PS5 the other day, we noticed other retailers stating the 11th instead, so it's no surprise that it's showing up in the wild.

The first unboxing video for GTA 6 seemingly arrived overnight, racking up over 1 million views already on social media since it was posted. This specific video is for the PS5 version, but we expect no major differences for the Xbox version.

Since this was posted, other unboxing videos have also started to hit the web, like you see in the YouTube video at the top of this article. It clearly shows that GTA 6 comes with a download code, a separate code for Ultimate Edition content where applicable, and a double-sided poster as had been confirmed previously.

It also now affirms that the poster contains the GTA 6 cover art on the front, and a piece of artwork for a female character on the back - not Lucia or Jason, but presumably a character that's heavily involved in the story regardless.

We've obviously talked a bit about the physical edition of GTA 6 already this week, and you can vote in the poll below if you didn't get a chance the first time, but we thought an actual unboxing video was worth a bit of extra coverage - an opportunity to see exactly what you'll be getting inside the physical edition if you've opted for it.

#4132. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

#4131. Skyrim Celebrates 15th Anniversary with Creation Club DLC Bundle, Big Sales, and More

The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim is officially 15 years old today, having originally launched on the 11th November, 2011.

And no, Bethesda doesn't have a new re-release lined up or anything like that, so the memes will have to be put on hold for now.

But that doesn't mean the developer's forgotten about its most successful RPG. To celebrate the occasion, it's reduced Skyrim: Special Edition's price by 80% on PS5 and PS4, cutting it all the way down to $7.99 / £6.99.

Buyers can then upgrade to the Anniversary Edition, which, as far as I can tell, still costs $19.99 / £15.99. Anniversary Edition is the one that bundles all of the Creation Club stuff into the deal.

If you somehow haven't played Skyrim before, or you've just never got around to it on PS5, it's a decent discount — although it's also worth pointing out that the Special Edition is currently available through a PS Plus Extra subscription as well.

Next up, Bethesda's curated a Creations (premium mods verified by the developer) bundle for the anniversary. It throws together five of the most highly rated Creations available at a heavily discounted price.

If you were to buy all of these Creations separately, they'd set you back 3,000 credits — roughly $28 / £27, since you have to buy separate 'Creation Credits' packs.

This bundle is going for 1,500 credits, which amounts to buying 500 and 1,000 Creation Credits at $15 / £14.

Obviously Skyrim's fan-crafted DLCs aren't everyone's cup of tea, but some of them really do fall in line with what you'd expect of an official release. Legacy of Orsinium in particular is a borderline expansion, and it's got a lot of fans.

Beyond all of this, The Elder Scrolls Online is unsurprisingly getting in on the action. You can unlock Skyrim-themed rewards by taking part in the MMO's current 'Golden Pursuit' campaign.

"Fans can also expect a week full of giveaways, community spotlights, and social content," Bethesda's press release adds.

When was the last time you played Skyrim? Dare I ask if you'll be venturing back to its snowy lands for this anniversary? Shout at something in the comments section below.

#4130. Japanese Charts: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Physical Takes The Lion's Share Of Its Japanese Sales

After Nintendo's reveal this week that The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time had shifted 5.2 million units in its first four days, it will come as no surprise to hear that it's a smash hit in Japan. But still, Famitsu's latest numbers are in, and the physical is flying!

According to this week's chart, Link's latest produced ~537,000 physical sales in its chart debut — giving it the lion's share of Japan's 810,000 sales that Nintendo reported, and leaving around 273,000 sales for digital. As we say, it's hardly surprising, but still!

It makes all the other entries this week look piddly by comparison. Nintendo Switch Sports Resort and Rhythm Heaven Groove round out the podium with a comparatively tiny 16,621 and 8,793 sales, respectively, and Stellar Blade: Complete Edition made its debut in fourth.

While Switch 2 sales are actually down following last week's bump, the console still leads this week's hardware chart by a comfortable margin. Nintendo's latest pulled in an additional ~53,000 sales this week, topping the PS5 Digital Edition, which came in with 11,377.

Once again, however, those Digital Edition sales swing things in Sony's favour over the Switch 1 when we look at the total SKU numbers for the week. The three PS5 systems combined this time for 11,699, while the Switch 1 units came in at 5,148.

#4129. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#4128. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#4127. Xbox Brings Halo's Iconic Pelican To Microsoft Flight Sim 2024 As Limited-Time Freebie

Act fast and claim the combat dropship for free!

Asobo Studios is commemorating the 25th anniversary of Halo by introducing the iconic UNSC Pelican into Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024.

Over the years, the combat dropshop has seen a plethora of talented pilots don its cockpit: Carol 'Foehammer' Rawley, the reluctant Fernando Esparza, and now you!

"Designed and built by Misriah Armory, the D77 Pelican has a typical crew of three (pilot, copilot, and crew chief) and can carry up to 14 fully outfitted infantry and their equipment. A vehicle can be carried in the external hardpoint clamp for immediate deployment. It has a lifting body design powered by four high-efficiency fusion thrusters with secondary positional / stability augmenters. The wings have three hardpoints each, which can hold sensors, cargo pods, or weapons."

Halo turns 25 alongside Xbox this Sunday, on November 15. So, we've seen iteration after iteration of the sci-fi shooter's most recognisable ship, which has traditionally only been pilotable in the previous MSFS and Halo 4's 'Shutdown' mission. There are other, more difficult means, to cheese your way into flying the Pelican across other Halo games, but now you don't have to.

The D77-TC Pelican in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 offers:

Personally, even though MSFS isn't my cup of tea, getting to roleplay what it'd been like to ferry Master Chief across the ring is something I'm definitely interested in trying. I really do enjoy when Halo vehicles show up in other games. From time to time, I stick on Halo 2's scorpion mix, hop into Forza Horizon 5 and take the Warthog for a spin. Just for the vibes.

If you're keen to fly the Halo Pelican in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, you'd best act quick, because it's only free between November 10-17, and then $9.99 afterwards.

#4126. Henry Cavill says it was "such an honor" to play Superman and is open to returning as the Man of Steel

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Henry Cavill would play the Man of Steel again

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Henry Cavill has said he's open to playing Superman again. The former Man of Steel actor was asked about the possibility amidst the news of upheaval at DC Studios as Peter Safran and James Gunn step down as heads.

"Look, there's lots of fantastic storylines," Cavill replied when asked if he'd don the suit again by Inverse. "There's always a lot of opportunity. As the pigeon sang to Fievel in An American Tail, 'never say never.' And I buy into that. I've had such a wonderful time playing Superman in the past. I would never say never now."

The former DC actor also shared a sweet story about how playing the superhero still impacts his daily life. "Sometimes people send my daughter Superman stuff as a joke," he explained. "Just the other day, we opened this Superman toy, and she looked at it and said, 'It's Dada!' She's only two years and four months, so no idea how she knows that's me; what kind of cosmic connection that was. But it really touched my heart in a special way, because obviously playing Superman was such an honor."

Currently, Superman is played by David Corenswet, who has appeared in two movies: Superman and Supergirl. He's set to reprise the role in the upcoming Man of Tomorrow, but it's not yet clear if that will be his final appearance.

In a statement about his exit, Gunn said that the characters he created will live on. However, other reports have suggested that under new leadership, DC will be rebooted once again. Jeremy Latcham, DC Studios' new head, has yet to lay out an official plan but has spoken in the past about his approach to movies being governed by his grandmother.

#4125. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#4124. Poll: 15 Years Later, Is Skyrim Still One of the Best Open World RPGs Out There?

11/11/11 — the famous release date that will forever be associated with The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim.

If you haven't already realised, today marks the title's 15th anniversary, and it's crazy to think that the open world RPG remains one of the most consistently popular games out there.

Indeed, at the time of writing this article, Skyrim's racking up around 40,000 concurrent players on Steam. Again, it's 15 years old!

There's no denying that Skyrim has a unique magic to it; an atmosphere, a sense of time and place. Bethesda struck absolute gold with this one, despite its often obvious flaws as a role-playing excursion.

Of course, the fact that Skyrim's simply never been replaced probably bolsters its legacy. The wait for The Elder Scrolls 6 has felt eternal at points, and the long, long awaited sequel is reportedly still years away from release.

I mean, would you be at all surprised if we got a PS6 port of Skyrim before Sentinel's arrival?

But Skyrim also owes so much of its longevity to its players. Modders have kept the candle burning for over a decade, and people are still forging ahead with extremely ambitious projects today.

No game maintains that level of interest without being special in the first place, however. I'd argue that even now, there's no open world RPG quite like Skyrim — it's a truly timeless experience with regards to its gameplay loop, dynamic happenings, and player-driven sense of adventure.

I've seen Skyrim dubbed Distractions: The Game, and that comedic description still rings true. I've lost track of how many times I've started a new Skyrim playthrough over the years, but somehow, it's never lost its appeal — and that's primarily because of how freeform it can feel.

But do you think Skyrim still stands tall as an all-timer RPG? Dare I ask if you're still playing it in 2026? Vote in our polls, and then tell me all about your wintry adventures in the comments section below.

Robert (or Rob if you're lazy) is an assistant editor of Push Square, and has been a fan of PlayStation since the 90s, when Tekken 2 introduced him to the incredible world of video games. He still takes his fighting games seriously, but RPGs are his true passion. The Witcher, Persona, Dragon Quest, Mass Effect, Final Fantasy, Trails, Tales — he's played 'em all. A little too much, some might say.

I think time hasn't been kind to Skyrim (and Bethesda in general) due to games such as The witcher 3, Cyberpunk 2077 and Baldur's gate having better character interactions and world building, but when it came out Skyrim was a revelation, and easily one of the best games of the PS3/Xbox 360 generation

It's janky but still a great RPG and as Todd says:

Skyrim used to be my favorite RPG, but got dethroned by the Witcher 3. That said, there's something magical about Skyrim. Even though the game clearly shows its age, it's just greater than the sum of its parts. There's something timeless about the vibe of the game. Skyrim is still the best game of its genre.

Yeah, yeah, the Witcher 3 (and Witcher 2, which honestly deserves to be brought up far more than it is) has a better main quest and more complete side quests, but the Witcher games are third person RPGs, which does make a bit of a difference in feel. Also, you’re playing as Geralt very clearly, whereas Skyrim, it’s a game where you have so much personal decision as to who the character is.

Yes, Elden Ring, BotW/Totk, and Red Dead 2 have all improved on the immersive open world, but, again, Skyrim is a first person game and you’ve got far more agency in character creation.

Yes, you could argue that Baldur’s Gate 3 has more agency in creation, but, again, there’s something to be said about the first person perspective.

And, with Cyberpunk, you’re playing as V, not as your own very personal character. And honestly, I know there’s a lot of love out there for Cyberpunk, but I cannot divorce my experience of it from its launch status, which was more a comedy than a tragedy of sorts, but it’s not a game I have the love for that others have.

Do Oblivion and Morrowind have better main quests? Oh, absolutely. Fallout 3 and New Vegas may hold that honor as well. And, yet… there’s still something just a little bit more immersive about Skyrim. Fallout 4 didn’t quite replicate it and neither did Starfield.

What it is is the storysensing. Skyrim is the absolute master of this craft. Storytelling is a far more familiar concept, where you’re interpreting a story that you’re meant to experience, but storysensing is the concept of absorbing enough details in a game’s world that you personally tell yourself your character’s story. You subconsciously fill things in and create things mentally in the game that don’t exist, but mesh into the world. You become a character wholly of your own existence as you play and you experience quests as that imagined being would experience them. You choose good or evil. You choose to fulfill your destiny as Dragonborn or not. You choice the guilds you work with, to become a werewolf, a vampire, etc. And it holds up remarkably well today too. And even just a moment back in its world is strangely still as inviting and absorbing as it was all those years ago now. And let me also say that the game has an immense pull with all people, not just those of us that are dedicated gamers. Skyrim was the first game that my wife ever really loved and is likely the only game she will ever hit 100+ hours in. I’ll be honest and say it’s probably my only and last 1000+ hour game. My son is now able to sink into the game and appreciate its majesty and it’s not so complex a game, as many of the other games I’ve listed, that he is repelled from the game pretension. The game understands that it’s a game for everyone. It’s a classic, an all-timer, and it was obvious 15 years ago and it still is today.

Skyrim’s one of the greatest games of all time. Certainly in my personal top 10 list of games of all time. It does have its flaws, but they’re strangely something easy to overlook. I do find the main quest to have quite a weak third act, but yet I’ve been compelled to complete it more times than games with far “better” storylines. And perhaps time had been kind enough to give us some absolutely essential DLCs that do provide deeper storytelling that present epilogues just as immersive as base game. Skyrim is, basically, to video games what the Beatles were to rock music. You can argue why you think it’s overrated, but at the end of the day, it delivers so many hits and everything is so memorable, even though you can see its influences. Todd Howard was right back then when he said, “It just works.” It may have been buggy at times, but he was certainly right.

#4123. Nintendo Reveals Switch 2 Black Friday Deals (US)

Nintendo has revealed a bunch of offers in the US for this year's Black Friday in a hope to boost its sales ahead of the holiday season.

The headline here is a Switch 2 hardware bundle, which contains the console, a digital copy of Mario Kart World, and a 3-month individual membership to Nintendo Switch Online. Priced at $499.99, this effectively wipes out the $50 price hike we saw earlier this year. This discount will be applicable from 22nd November to 5th December.

From 22nd November to 29th November, you can also bag $20 off the suggested retail price of select first-party games, including Donkey Kong Bananza and Super Mario Galaxy + Super Mario Galaxy 2.

All of these offers will be available at Nintendo New York and Nintendo San Fransisco alongside select retailers. A Black Friday eShop sale will also kick off from 19th November, so keep an eye on Nintendo Life for our recommendations when the time comes.

Nintendo recently confirmed that the Switch 2 has surpassed 26 million console sales, despite a drop of around 37% year-on-year. The recent launch of Ocarina of Time will no doubt boost console sales nicely, as the game itself has already sold over 5 million copies.

#4122. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#4121. Shrek 2 Remastered Has No Official Reviews Yet, But The User Reviews Are Quite Bizarre

It has a high score on Xbox right now, but a Mixed one on Steam

Yesterday marked the launch of Shrek 2 Remastered on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S (along with other platforms), and if you're wondering why nobody seems to be talking about it, it's because there are no official reviews yet.

It seems codes were only sent out at launch for this one, which means it's going to take a while for the critics to catch up and share their thoughts on this remaster of an original Xbox cult classic.

We can at least see what the initial user reviews are saying about it though, and if you look at the Xbox Store, everything seems to be pretty rosy. Shrek 2 Remastered has a 4.3/5 rating on the US Xbox Store as things stand, with 76% of people giving it a 5-star review, while most of the (minimal) grumbles are focused on bugs and crashes.

The Steam reviews for Shrek 2 Remastered are quite bizarre though. Over there, the game currently has a "Mixed" average rating based on over 350 user reviews, with 46% of people rating it "Positive" overall.

If you look at the "Most Helpful" reviews that appear first, there are multiple people suggesting it's not a great port, highlighting issues with bugged cutscenes, a lack of settings options, and even claims that the CPUs are less intelligent than they were in the original game (although others debate that it plays "exactly the same" as it used to!). There are also multiple accusations that the remaster might have been partially put together using generative AI, although this is just speculation and not confirmation by any means.

Some people are totally put off by all these issues, while others are still really enjoying their time with the game.

Satan Claus on Steam: "Shrek 2 was one of my favourite games growing up, and I honestly can't explain how happy I am to have the chance to play it again after all these years. It's just as special as I remember, and seeing it brought back with changes that do the original justice is wonderful. Even better, being able to enjoy it on modern hardware, especially the Steam Deck, feels like a dream come true. Some childhood memories are worth revisiting, and this is absolutely one of them."

Mikey on Steam: "I was really hyped for this remaster since this game is a game I grew up playing with my sister, but I am sort of disappointed with the state it is in right now. Lots of camera bugs, cutscenes ending aprubtly, missing skybox textures, characters looking woody and uncanny and lots more. It's like they just threw a paint bucket on it and called it a day. I'll wait for patches, since there still is hope."

As mentioned, Shrek 2 Remastered is getting a much better reception on Xbox than Steam right now, so perhaps we ended up getting the better version (or Xbox fans are more lenient), and you can check it out for yourself at the price of £22.49 / $26.99 for Series X and Series S if you're interested.

We do actually have a review copy of the game that we'll hopefully be able to check out soon, so stay tuned for our impressions in the near future. We'll also keep an eye out for raw Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S footage comparisons so you can get an idea of how it plays across both consoles.

For now though, we'll leave you with some basic gameplay from Shrek 2 Remastered down below.

#4120. Constantine director Francis Lawrence thinks a Keanu Reeves sequel can happen now James Gunn has left DC

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Unlock instant access to exclusive member features.

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

Francis Lawrence says "the people that were at DC were an impediment to us making" Constantine 2

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While fans worry about the state of DC after news of James Gunn and Peter Safran's exit, there may be some light at the end of the tunnel, as the shakeup has made Constantine director Francis Lawrence believe that a sequel can actually happen now.

"Not that I want anybody to lose their jobs… but I will say that we’ve been trying to make Constantine 2 for 20-something years, and we have an idea, and we have a script, and we’ve been wanting to make it," said Lawrence to Collider, "and the people that were at DC were an impediment to us making it. So, we are now more hopeful as of yesterday’s news that maybe now there will be another opportunity."

Lawrence added, "There’s always been obstacles in the road to making it, and it’s not me, it’s not Keanu, it’s not Akiva. J.J. [Abrams] is on it, as well. We all want to do it. So, it’s really going to be people at Paramount, Warner, whoever’s running DC now, getting everybody on board to say, like, 'Hey, we can do a sequel of our version of Constantine.'"

On November 9, it was announced that Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as DC Studios co-CEOs on December 1, 2026, just over four years after they were hired. The pair will be replaced by former Marvel Studios executive Jeremy Latcham. This comes not long after Skydance-owned Paramount acquired Warner Bros. and all it owns, including HBO, DC Studios, and various franchises.

Released in 2005, Constantine loosely adapts DC Comics' Hellblazer series, following Keanu Reeves as cynical exorcist John Constantine, who can travel between the realms of life and death. But when he is approached by Rachel Weisz's detective to help investigate her twin sister's death, Constantine unravels a conspiracy where demons are trying to enter the real world. The movie was actually Lawrence's directorial debut, before he went on to helm such titles as The Hunger Games and I Am Legend.

The last we heard of the sequel is that it is still in early development, with Evil Dead Wrath's Francis Galluppi penning the script. No plot details have been revealed at this time. But tt's not just the Constantine sequel that is up in the air right now, as it is not clear what will happen to the rest of the DC projects currently in the works. Reports suggest the company plans to "dismantle" Gunn's DCU: Chapter One.

For more, check out our guide on how to watch the DC movies in order, and keep up with upcoming DC movies and shows announced before Gunn's departure.

#4119. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#4117. 'We Will Put In Our Best Efforts To Develop For It' - Stellar Blade CTO Wants Xbox Helix Dev Kit

"Personally, I am looking forward to the next-gen Xbox"

Shift Up CTO DongKi Lee, best known for his work on Stellar Blade and the studio's mobile games, recently spoke at a developer panel about his excitement to get hands-on with Xbox Project Helix development kits. All whilst in front of a senior official of team Xbox.

As Inven Global puts it, Lee was one of five panellists, comprised of execs from other development studios, and answered questions on what it's like developing games for console in the Korean gaming industry.

When asked about what advantages the console platforms have compared to PC, fellow panellist and former Tekken CEO Katsuhiro Harada took the opportunity to throw some shade at the Xbox Series S, jesting "I wish hardware like the 'Xbox Series S' wouldn't be released", attributing additional development resources to optimising games for the lower spec console.

In response to this, the Shift Up CTO spoke about his excitement to work alongside Xbox and his eagerness to see Project Helix developer kits in Korea:

"Personally, I am looking forward to the next-gen Xbox 'Helix'. From an engineer's standpoint, if you provide us with a dev kit first in Korea as early as possible, we will put in our best efforts to develop for it."

Xbox players have been asking for a Stellar Blade port for quite some time, regularly mocking up fake Xbox Series box art and posting it to socials, and usually asking when Shift Up will bring the game to Microsoft hardware. It's certainly a possibility, and DongKi Lee's enthusiasm for working with Project Helix is encouraging. That, and this tweet from Edo, Shift Up's 'publishing guy':

During the panel, Lee was asked about the recent Switch 2 version of Stellar Blade and the effort involved in porting the game from PS5 to NS2. The Shift Up CTO shared a chuckle with the panel moderator and CEO Harada whilst discussing what could and couldn't be compromised during the port. Specifically, how reducing the polygon count on protagonist Eve's 'rear' was "never an option".

@themightyant If they release a Helix S or something similar, it would be very different from the Series S from a developer's perspective. If I've understood things correctly, the Xbox Helix OS will be much closer to a Windows PC environment. That would mean developers wouldn't need to create a specific port for the Helix S, just like PC developers don't make a separate version of a game for every possible hardware configuration.

It would basically come down to a different settings profile that's optimized for the hardware. That's essentially how games work on devices like the Xbox ROG Ally. Developers don't make a special version for it, it's the exact same PC version, with only the configuration and performance settings changing.

I don't know exactly what the Helix OS will look like in the end, but there will almost certainly be a greater level of standardization between PC and Xbox games. #4116. Resident Evil Requiem Wins the First 2026 Game of the Year Award

Top accolade at the Golden Joystick Awards

Resident Evil Requiem has been crowned the Ultimate Game of the Year at the Golden Joystick Awards, the first major games award ceremony of 2026.

Alongside the biggest award, it was also named the Console Game of the Year, and it won categories celebrating the best lead performer (Angela Sant'Albano as Grace Ashcroft) and the best game trailer. Most of the Golden Joystick Awards are decided by a public vote, and the race for Ultimate Game of the Year was extremely close.

Resident Evil Requiem won the award with 17% of the overall vote, but Phantom Blade Zero was right behind it with 16% and then Crimson Desert got 15%.

Obviously, since it's not out yet, GTA 6 wasn't eligible for any categories.

Elsewhere, the award for the Best Remake / Remaster went to The Witcher 3 Remastered, then Dispatch won the Best Soundtrack and Best Storytelling categories. Onimusha: Way of the Sword has the Best Audio Design according to the voters, Valheim was the year's Best Indie Game, and The Witcher 4 is the Most Wanted Game.

Do you agree with the winners at the Golden Joystick Awards? Share your reaction in the comments below.

#4115. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

Andy Serkis provides an exciting update on The Hunt for Gollum

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Andy Serkis has confirmed filming has wrapped on The Hunt for Gollum.

"We've just wrapped principal photography and directing [The Hunt for Gollum]," Serkis – who is directing the latest Lord of the Rings movie, as well as portraying Gollum once more – said on The Morning Mosh Pit (H/T Polygon). "It's been an incredible journey back into an endlessly complex and wonderfully drawn and written character."

The Hunt for Gollum, set largely between The Hobbit and Lord of the Rings trilogies, sees Smeagol in desperate search for The One Ring, with Strider/Aragorn sent by Gandalf to track the creature down.

While Gollum is undoubtedly one of the most memorable and uniquely tragic things in The Lord of the Rings, Serkis has professed his excitement at digging deeper into the psyche of the character.

"I'm very excited about it," Serkis said. "He is one of Tolkien's most complex characters, and it definitely bears further examination."

The Hunt for Gollum will bring back a handful of familiar faces alongside Serkis' iconic Gollum, including Sir Ian McKellen's Gandalf, Elijah Wood's Frodo, and Lee Pace's Thranduil. Aragorn has been recast, with Jamie Dornan playing a younger version of the character. Newcomers to the franchise include Kate Winslet, Anya Taylor-Joy, and Leo Woodall.

The Hunt for Gollum courted controversy earlier this year with the admission AI was used in some of the de-aging, but Serkis told Variety, "We're not creating AI shots in our movie," and that "Every shot is created in a traditional way."

The Hunt for Gollum hits cinemas on December 17, 2027.

#4113. Talking Point: What's Your Favourite Tiny Tweak In Zelda: Ocarina Of Time?

While the Ocarina of Time we see on Switch 2 is undoubtedly the same game we all know from the N64, there are enough tweaks in there that have had the biggest fans amongst us clicking and pointing at the screen like that Leonardo DiCaprio meme.

We're not talking about the big changes, either. You can keep your new visuals, fancy jump buttons and modern camera controls; we're getting excited over new floor textures and wall decals — stuff that wouldn't stand out unless you had played the original more times than you care to admit.

Below, we have shared our favourite tiny tweaks that have stood out so far. Some are more niche than others, but these are the little changes that had us beaming in our first few hours of rediscovering Hyrule and finding it not quite as we remember it.

After you've read through our picks, why not head to the comments and share your top tweaks?

Knowing the original game like the back of my hand, I'm yet to walk into a room without going, "Oooh, look how they changed that bit!" But the one that has stood out to me the most so far is being able to ride Epona right up to the entrance to Kakariko Village without getting chucked off at the bottom of the stairs.

Does it change the game in any way at all? Absolutely not. But praise be to whichever innovative dev at Nintendo thought, 'What if Jim didn't have to sit through a backtracking animation every time he forgot to dismount quickly enough?'

The ragdoll may not be a substantial inclusion, but if I can pick between a stiff, canned animation of Link collapsing to the floor and seeing his lifeless body tumble into the rapids that lead up to Zora's Domain, you know what I'm going to choose.

The option to remove one of the few tweaks I haven’t enjoyed so far — Navi’s incessant dialogue boxes commenting on everything — is a godsend. I was concerned she’d spend the entire game puncturing the mood with “Oooh, big mountain!” and “Wow, great work!” and “OMG, that was a lucky escape!” (I’m paraphrasing, but that’s the gist), and she does.

Turning on the ‘Master’ display option, though, reduces the UI to the bare minimum, removing almost everything, including Navi’s dialogue boxes. So when I emerge onto Hyrule Field, the landscape speaks for itself (with a little help from the music). Bliss. Other people might enjoy her interjections, and yes, I will miss a cute line or two, but thanks for letting me turn off the running commentary, Nintendo.

Turning Grouch Mode off, the slingshot easter egg in the courtyard window is ace. And Kakariko feels more like a real place now. And those little rivulets on Hyrule Field add so much. And that part of Lon Lon... *babbling trails off...

Without heading into spoiler territory, I suppose my niche tweak (if it’s considered niche) would be the addition of Threads of Time, but more specifically the Tapestry.

I’ve filled out my tapestry now, but throughout each stage of Link’s journey it was nice to see the progress I was making. I jumped into the remake with the hope of experiencing it with fresh eyes (although I’d played the original), and it really felt like it at times. It was also a really good way for me to gauge what I could do next should I forget, collectables I likely still needed, or even secrets I still had to unlock.

It’s a very simple addition common in modern gaming, but a tweak which was needed.

I’m enjoying all the revamped music, but one arrangement that took me by surprise is when you encounter common or garden foes. There’s more urgency and danger now: notes are sharply cutting in, there’s a subtle, unnerving rise and fall in volume, and if the battle lasts long enough, it goes up a notch when a horn (I’m guessing!) is eventually layered on top.

For a track I hadn’t given a second’s thought to in the original, I’m now delighted every time an enemy nears.

Note. Very minor pre-Hyrule Field spoilers ahead...

Some of the subtle tweaks to Ocarina of Time’s narrative landed so well with me. I won’t go into the later examples, but I absolutely adored the moment when Link runs into both Mido and Saria after leaving the Deku Tree.

Mido, who feels much more fleshed out in the remake, expresses shock and immediate concern for the Deku Tree, while Saria is devastated at the thought of Link leaving Kokiri Forest. She leaves, heartbroken at Link’s decision, and it’s only when we exit the forest that she catches up to make amends and deliver the Fairy Ocarina.

This extra scene isn’t much in the grand scheme of things, but it really adds weight to Link’s departure, emphasising the home and friends that he’ll be leaving behind. I love it.
