There's much less "how was I supposed to know?" moments. On one hand it's more accessible, on the other hand it's less cryptic and mysterious when you stumble into something, or learn from another source. These were always the smaller things that you didn't need to do to beat the game, anyway.

My favorite tweak is how they made Link leaving the cutscene where he gets the Fairy Ocarina more impactful.

In the original, he takes a couple tentative steps back, then leaves using his normal running animation. You could interpret it as emotional, but it could’ve also been just him walking away since it’s the normal movement animation.

I like that they emphasized that small detail by making it more obviously emotional in the way Link leaves. Just a small detail that reinterprets the original material in a way that I thought they might have been going for, but was unclear due to hardware limitations.

@bluemujika 70? Someone didn't get to buy it from Walmart or Amazon for 60

Cutscenes in general are much improved while keeping the tone of the original. Link getting knocked TF out by Darunia had me in stitches. Ruto (especially in Japanese had the Ojousama mannerisms dialed up while somehow making her sound …less spoiled?), just Ruto. Anytime they lean on Zelda being a badarse is always a plus in my book and woo she’s even cooler y’all while still having an air of vulnerability and gravitas. They over did her guilt a bit though. Loved Impa as usual and Nabooru felt more like a warrior for justice this time around (she has never liked Ganondorf, but she really felt he didn’t deserve blind praise simply because he was their king due to a genetic quirk). They made Mido somewhat decent. I am anti bully and feel those types of people don't change, but I sorta felt bad for Mido.

I have never hated Navi, but I teared up when she left at the end. I really enjoyed hanging out with that little lightbulb. When you meet a great fairy her comment on the fountain made me laugh. You could almost hear her trying to figure out to become a great fairy. I do miss her hanging out in Link’s hat though.

I’ll admit muscle memory makes me not try a lot of stuff so I tend to notice scene changes, but I agree with bringing Epona to the gate. My eyebrows went up at that. Grottos are way easier to find (thank you!). I don’t like that redeads run at you now. F that. Somehow Dark Link feels like more of an ahole?

Morpha boss fight was fun this time. (As was Ganon). And the shadow and camera angle was good for my visually impaired self. I was concerned. I spend too much time reflecting back beamos lasers.

Also whomever designed new dead hand? Yeah I wanna cuss that person out.

My favorite though? THE ZORA ARE FREE (and all have the flu but still…)!!

How that stupid Owl doesnt ask if you understand, ITS THE BEST!!

Oh definitely the little tassels on Ganondorf's armour.

If I'm being serious, I liked that new item that allowed you to summon a business scrub at will. Didn't think I'd actually use them but they came in handy in a pinch.

The extra bits of context in the cutscenes are great. The story just makes more sense with them.

Just finished a 100% play through today and I have to say i'm mighty impressed.

I went back to play the original for the first time after beating the remake. Besides the obvious improvements like camera controls, being able to save and quit and be in the same area is game-changing. The first time I saved in the original was in Kakariko and when I opened the game to be back in Link's house, I was pretty peeved...

Also after dying to the big octorock and having to run back to the boss room every time with only 3 hearts, that was pretty annoying but I'm not sure if it works like that in the remake considering how few times I died. OoT64 is definitely harder, but i think it comes from the single stick control more than actual difficulty changes in the remake

Also one little note, I did see a lot of bad-faith haters complaining about the changed dialogue, but I have honestly enjoyed the original writing and lack of shoddy voice acting in the original more than the remake so far. It does kinda feel like they watered it down for the remake, and the voice acting does not help that at all... even if the cutscenes are pretty

@solarwolf07 Yeah, it's kind of funny how a lot of the difficulty change feels like it's mostly just due to the controls and camera being so much easier so you're not constantly getting merced by flaming bats you can't get the camera to focus on or whatever. It feels like you actually get fewer hearts and fairies and stuff in dungeons so I don't think it's like the game constantly giving you health that it didn't previously (aside from the fairy thoughts, if you get those).

The fact that you can wear masks as an adult! I actually specifically asked for this in a thread a couple weeks ago. Now I don't have to go back to child form every time I come across a new gossip stone just to find out what it says. And of course I can read everyone's thoughts in the future to find out how they have changed.

The emotional beats between link and saria are tweaked just enough, that my god. It just hits you like a bus. Even when you just talk to her at her spot outside the forest temple, that sense of leaving childhood is so intense in a way I did not expect

Probably thawing Zora's Domain. Nothing of substance to do there afterward which is why I'd consider it tiny but it was a big loose end to leave in the original and it's nice having the quick access tunnel from Lake Hylia working as an adult.

The movement, this is the best any character has controlled in possibly any game I've ever played. I was very worried that they were going to introduce momentum based movement like how characters control in more realistic AAA games (Uncharted for example seems to be the template for this and many other games in the same vain). But Link has a bit of that at the start of his run but they kept it very arcade like where any direction he goes is almost instant, combine that with being able to walk over any terrain and perform jumps and acrobatics in the environment and you're left with a result that enhances the greatest game of all time to an even higher level. The longer I played the game the more impressed I became with how intuitive it was to control Link and cannot praise the work the developers did enough.

For me it's Navi extra dialogue, sorry to disagree Gavin. But her having extra flavortext makes her feel more like a character than a tool to explain and target enemies. And now that she feels more like an individual the game feels like your playing it with a buddy! I even used her more not for actual help but because i was curious as to what she had to say.

I like that the Mask of Truth can actually be used to read minds now! It's not just backstory flavour, it functions like that for the player too.

@Ryu_Niiyama I really like how all the Zora caught a cold because they have been frozen 😄

@EarthboundBenjy Also just the fact that it can be worn as adult Link. You encounter and can speak to so many more of the gossip stones through just playing the game instead of having to back track as a child.

I like that the Gerudo's are a little more aggressive and mindful of their surroundings now. It made finding the carpenters more challenging!

The Cuccos thing is slightly harder as you now have to remember to jump. Along with loads of other bits being harder if your a dum dum and forget to jump. Some changes like the volley bit and the 2nd dungeon boss as child link are easier. And most of the time when you forget to jump and get punished your not even that annoyed about it and enjoy the challenge of remember to jump lol.

Haven't played a whole lot yet, but the lack of loading screens between buildings and most areas is pretty cool, and something I was hoping for. Being able to see into Lon Lon Ranch from Hyrule Field and then walk right in is pretty damn cool.

I like when you find Richard, the fat lady lets you ride her around Hyrule Town to say thanks

All replaying it has done for me is to wish there’s a new Zelda made in the same format. An “ocarina 2” if you like.

I love BotW and ToTK but damn this old setup is a joy to play. The old dungeons, creativity everywhere. It’s nice not having a stamina bar and a condensed world for a change. This to me really FEELS like a Zelda, much more than the new open world games do.

I'm only at Goron City (really taking my time to absorb everything) but so far, it's definitely the music. I don't know if that qualifies as a tiny tweak, but it truly makes the game even more special. I can't get enough.

There’s chanting in the music for the fire temple again. Albeit somewhat different than the original score

Poor Navi. She just can't catch a break, even if her interjections are just little speech bubbles now. Eternally cursed. lol

My number one favorite change is the orchestral score. It really goes hard, even when pushing/pulling the master sword. But yeah Nintendo knocked it out of the universe with this. WOW.

Lmao… for a moment I read “who’s your favorite tiny twink?” … and I was da fck?

Also… the most important one that couldn’t be done in the original. The Zora are free at last!

@ChromaticDracula The orchestral versions of the music are OUTSTANDING! I'm always curious how nobody seems to mention this...

My favourite minor tweak is that the hookshot can hit those eye switches now. That means you can legitimately do water temple first if you want. Good change.

My least favourite tweak is how they've streamlined dungeons by taking out locks and keys. They don't feel as difficult or labyrinthian now.

@Aurumonado I always did water temple first ...Gotta rescue the wife before the friend!

@DanElectrode very true. On the topic of heart drops, I noticed that heart drops in the original seem to spawn three instead of one, which pleasantly surprised me haha

I’m not going to go into specifics and spoil anything, but for me it’s post-Water Temple Zora Domain.

I just love the ability to jump. Feels like some Mario game sometimes because I jump like an idiot everywhere 🤣 Especially from rock to rock, really funny to do !

I did not play much of the original, so I can't compare extensively, but one aspect I really like too is the fact you can explore cities at night now ! Kokiri forest is so beautiful at this time of day !

Putting Din's Fire in the Death Mountain GFF rather than the hidden Hyrule Castle one.

Breath of the wild references love.But a fairy now only heals 6 hearts not full health hate.

Difficult to remember because I only played Zelda Ocarina once back in the day, and revisiting it in recent years I was confronted with a blurring, clunky mess and barely lasted an hour in it. The remake is a godsend for someone like me eager to experience it again without suffering the many archaic elements that present themselves today.

I mostly notice that everything feels nicer. There's none of the clunkiness whether that be in the controls, obviously a vastly improved frame rate, and general design tweaks. One that I did note is the narrow path in the Fire Temple where a fall meant a long walk all the way back to trying it again. Boring! Now, Link will cling to the ledge and recover, or will fall into a lava pit, lose health, and respawn.

I bet this is one of the petty examples that IGN used to say this version of Ocarina is "easier" in its obvious agenda to not score it a 10. Whereas to sane people, the punishment from that fall is purely cheap game design. The path is easy to traverse as long as it's not rushed, so clinging to the ledge or losing health is an excellent two-stage warning to be careful compared to the previous brutal method after some simple carelessness. That is much more in sync with the ethos of Ocarina whereas in something like Ghosts N Goblins, that sort of cheap punishment is to be expected!

There are a lot of little things I like. Pro / Master HUD is great. Jumping changes gameplay. The cutscenes are astonishing, especially the scene you get the master sword for the first time. The environment changes with the modern rendering makes everything feel more natural and true to their vision. And as others mentioned, the orchestral music is just beautiful.

All great but the best? It’s the three C’s. Character, Camera, and Controls for me.

We take it for granted but dual sticks and 100% camera control makes such a fundamental difference in the gameplay that I truly believe it will surprise many how it feels to go back to play the original. It just gives me even more freedom. Ocarina of Time was the first game I played on N64. It was my first 3D game and introduced me to “open worlds”. To now experience that with modern camera controls with all the other changes just really seals the deal for me. Link does what I want, when I want it, and how I want. I never feel cheated. I feel like when I run up and jump near Epona, it just works and Link mounts correctly. I like when I walk around with my shield up, he keeps walking forward but I can pivot my shield to the left or right. I can control my sword swing direction. I can swing the camera just where I need it and it doesn’t clip into the environment. They way Link responds to all my inputs just feels… right.

A lot of people will go back to the original. It was will still hold up very well, but all things considered, the camera controls makes the biggest difference to me. I can say so far, this is my favourite version of Ocarina of Time and I am surprised I feel this way. This game beat my expectations.

If I had any minor criticisms about the controls, it’s simply the fact I can’t be as hardcore as in the N64 version, and I don’t have a separate dedicated button to raise my shield while Z-targeting like in the original version.

They nailed the feeling of walking on ice! The frosting and the snow in the Ice Cavern is amazing. Actually made me reach for a blanket!

#4112. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

#4111. Two Major Developers Explain Why They Like And Dislike Making Games For Xbox Series S

"I wish hardware like the 'Xbox Series S' wouldn't be released (laughs)"

Over the years, we've heard all kinds of stories from all kinds of developers about whether they either like or dislike making games for the Xbox Series S, and former Tekken boss Katsuhiro Harada falls into the "dislike" category.

In a recent panel discussion that was transcribed by the folks at InvenGlobal, Harada noticed that a senior Xbox official was in the audience, and joked that he wanted to let them know how much he isn't a fan of the Xbox Series S.

"Since a senior Xbox official is actually in attendance here today, I wish hardware like the 'Xbox Series S' wouldn't be released (laughs)."

He then went on to explain that although the low memory is "an issue" of the Xbox Series S, the hardest part is that it's actually so similar to the Series X, but with "awkwardly lower performance". Harada also pointed out that players direct their complaints to the developers rather than Microsoft if they don't like the visuals and/or performance.

"Low memory is an issue, but the hardest part is that it's a device so similar to Series X while having awkwardly lower performance [...] Furthermore, in markets like the US, there are more Series S users than Series X users, so we can't just cut corners. Yet after launch, Series S users direct their complaints at us developers rather than Microsoft, asking "Why is texture resolution lower only on Series S?"

Finally, he also noted that developing for the Nintendo Switch 2 is actually easier in some ways because it's a "distinct device for Nintendo fans", whereas the Xbox Series S is akin to "having to do extra work for a slightly weaker child" compared to putting in your "absolute best output" for the Xbox Series X.

Despite what it might seem like, a lot of this conversation seemed to be very lighthearted and full of laughs, and when Cyberpunk 2077's Paweł Sasko stepped in to highlight the benefits of the Xbox Series S including its affordable price and the ability to better optimise for low-spec platforms, Harada admitted that he made it sound a lot more attractive.

In fact, it was so convincing that Harada jokingly worried that it might lead to a similar Project Helix alternative!

Director Paweł: "Harada speaks a lot of truth. Players don't fully understand the technical context behind why fewer characters appear on screen or why visuals are downgraded. However, intensely optimizing for lower-spec platforms definitely brings the benefit of making the game run significantly better across all platforms—including PS5, high-end PCs, and handhelds like Steam Deck and ROG Ally.

And the biggest advantage of Series S is that its affordable price makes it accessible. Not every gamer can buy expensive high-end hardware, so from a developer's perspective, even if the strict constraints are painful, there is a silver lining in expanding market penetration to deliver the game to more players."

CEO Harada: "Director Paweł packaged Series S so gracefully that the Microsoft representative in the audience keeps nodding along. I'm worried they'll feel reassured and release a successor like 'Helix S' for the next-gen Xbox as well (laughs)."

It's best not to take any of this too seriously, but it does at least highlight the differing opinions throughout the industry about whether the Xbox Series S was a good or bad idea in hindsight.

From a consumer perspective at least, we reckon it was a fantastic idea. The Xbox Series S has continually managed to deliver incredible-looking games over the past six years, and in a time where console prices are constantly on the up, the Series S at least provides a somewhat affordable current-gen hardware option - at least if you find a good deal.

#4110. 'You'll Own Nothing': Sony Wins Hall of Shame Award for Deciding to Kill Physical Discs

I can't imagine this is something Hermen Hulst will want to display on his mantelpiece: PlayStation and Sony have won a Hall of Shame award, called a Shonky Award, from an Australian outlet for its decision to stop making physical discs.

Choice, an Australian website, runs an annual Hall of Shame series, known as the Shonky Awards, where it highlights the "worst products and services uncovered by our experts this year". In 2026, PlayStation finds itself with a Shonky Award alongside Virgin Australia, Ticketmaster, and more companies.

This is because of the company's decision to end PlayStation disc production from January 2028, combined with its current EULA (End-User License Agreement) tied to digital game purchases. A lot of the Choice write-up focuses on the latter:

"In this age of instant gratification, it doesn’t get much more convenient than being able to easily download a movie or video game to your collection to start enjoying immediately," it opens with. "But will you be enjoying them for years to come? That’s less certain."

The site then continues: "Because, according to Sony Interactive Entertainment, you don’t actually own the movies and games that you buy as a digital download instead of a disc. Instead, you’re buying a licence to access the content via Sony’s various digital storefronts, such as the PlayStation Store."

News Sony Reminds PS5 Owners Their Digital Games Are Licensed, Not Sold

But Steam, Xbox, and Nintendo all say the same

News No Disc, No Buy and PS5 Blackout Protests Fail to Impact PlayStation

Active users increases, digital sales percentage increases

It speaks about how Sony still "owns your digital media", and how, in reality, you're actually buying a "long-term rental". Choice then points to the sudden removal of Studio Canal movies from the PS Store, where refunds weren't offered.

The decision to stop physical PlayStation discs is then discussed, with worries over digital ownership arising once more. It analyses the EULA once more, but as we've pointed out in the past, the terms of Sony's license agreement are virtually identical to that of Xbox, Nintendo, and PC platform Steam.

All their terms of use speak about how the content you're buying is a license — you don't own it. Allow me to reshare the research editor Sammy Barker put into his previous piece concerning the EULAs on other platforms:

The Content and Services are licensed, not sold. Your license confers no title or ownership in the Content and Services. To make use of the Content and Services, you must have a Steam Account and you may be required to be running the Steam client and maintaining a connection to the Internet.

All Digital Goods are licensed, not sold. Your right to access or use any Digital Good is subject to your compliance with: (a) all license terms, license limitations, codes of conduct, and payment terms in the Terms; (b) your payment in full for the applicable Digital Good; (c) these Rules, and; (d) any additional terms provided when you acquire your license.

Subject to the terms of this Agreement, Nintendo grants you a non-exclusive, revocable license to use the Software solely on the Console for your personal, non-commercial use. For clarity, the Software is licensed, not sold, to you, and you may not make use of the Software except as expressly authorized by this Agreement.

These all read very similarly and mean the exact same thing: on all the major video game platforms, you purchase a license to play a video game; you don't own the actual video game.

However, because Sony is removing the option of buying physical PlayStation discs in just over a year to channel all of its business into the PS Store, it's catching considerably more scrutiny than anyone else.

For that, PlayStation wins a Shonky Award from Choice.

"You can’t protect your licensed media based on the current EULA, and there won’t be any alternatives once the discs go away. You’ll own nothing," it concludes.

[source choice.com.au, via gamesradar.com]

Not all Steam games have DRM. GoG which was notably absent of a mention in the article has no DRM on it's games and come with extras (Wallpapers, artwork, soundtracks, manuals and other digital gubbins) . They're even bringing out a physical service where you can buy a physical copy of a game delivered to your door or download the files for box etc to print out for free.

Its always been this way - the terms haven't changed - the ONLY difference is that with Physical discs, that licence is embedded on that bit of plastic and you can sell, trade or let a friend borrow that Licence but with Digital, that licence is locked to your Digital account. Its a bit more tricky to block access to a Physical Licence but that hasn't stopped a number of games being 'unplayable' regardless of whether you bought a licence on disc or digitally - Destiny, Marvels Avengers, Anthem etc all now just coasters or 'landfill trash'.

What you purchase, as you always have, is a licence to access and use the Software belonging to a Publisher/developer on whatever platform you have. Just because you have a Licence to play BF6 on PS5, doesn't mean you can play on PC, Xbox or Steam as they'll sell you a licence to access that software on their Platform too.

Even back when games were supplied on Cartridges, you purchased a licence to play the Software loaded on to those cartridges. They obviously have to supply the software to you in some way so you can access it with your licence, but you don't 'own' the Software and if you tried to copy it and distribute it because you 'think' you own it, that's Piracy and always has been.

Not saying I agree with the way Digital is limiting customers ability to 'sell, trade or share' their Licence in the exact same way they can with Physical Not saying I am 'happy' that big Corporations are being more 'anti-consumer'. In theory, we 'should' own our Licences as we always have and should have the right to sell, trade etc but we've never owned the software and as games/hardware have become more integrated with the internet, its enabled the owners of that software/hardware to block or remove access. The Licence isn't as 'permanent' as it once was. You can still use your licence to play N64 games but many games or content aren't playable today even if you own the Disc because they've turned off the Servers - you can't play Killzone online anymore and like I said, can't play Destiny, Anthem or Marvels Avengers either whether you bought on disc or not.

#4109. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#4107. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#4105. Xbox Brings Its Free Tier Of Cloud Gaming To Loads More Players Today

You may recall that back in July, Xbox announced a new free version of Xbox Cloud Gaming that would allow you to play games at no charge, but you'd be forced to deal with ads as a compromise.

That tier of Xbox Cloud Gaming was in testing for months, but as of today (November 11th), it's rolled out publicly - meaning the vast majority of Xbox users around the world should now have access to it.

Xbox has been very quiet about it today so far, but based on what we've seen around the web, the free tier of Xbox Cloud Gaming will provide you with a 30-minute slot to stream "select games from your library" as well as select free-to-play games, after which time you'll be kicked off and will have to start a new session.

You'll see ads before the session begins, and seemingly never again throughout your 30-minute playtime.

"You can stream select games for free by watching ads before each gaming session. Session time limits apply. After a session ends, you can watch another set of ads to start a new session."

News Xbox Introduces Free Game Streaming With Ads, Outlines Five Principles They'll Adhere To

Rolling out now as a "test" for Xbox Insiders

Despite the rapid session length, this could prove a popular option for anyone who wants to play GTA 6 on Xbox One (for example) without being forced to pay anything for Xbox Cloud Gaming. We'd urge some caution for now though, as Xbox has yet to confirm whether GTA 6 will be one of the "select" games that supports this feature.

Meanwhile, the cloud playtime limits that were announced a while ago for Xbox Game Pass members have now started kicking in, which also means you can now purchase "Cloud Playtime" to top it up if you run out.

The prices for this here in the UK are as follows:

Curiously though, I've checked the new "Cloud Playtime" option in the Settings menu on my Xbox Series X and I'm being informed that I've still got "Unlimited" access to Xbox Cloud Gaming with my Ultimate membership, so it might be worth checking the same thing on your end and seeing what it says for you.

I'm not the only person who's spotted something similar:

Anyway, we've thrown Xbox's official tweet up above, and you can hit the link in it to find out even more details.

#4104. 'There Is No Truth to These Claims': Marvel 1943 Not Cancelled, But Doesn't Sound Great

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra – the highly promising superhero game starring Captain America and Black Panther – has not been cancelled, despite rumours to the contrary earlier today.

A fan account claimed on X (or Twitter) that the project, fronted by former Uncharted lead Amy Hennig, had been scrapped. That post has since been deleted.

But Kotaku gained access to a message posted in dev Skydance Games’ private Slack channel, where executive producer Lu Gigliotti confirmed with leadership that the reports aren’t true.

The game – first announced in 2019 – was originally due out earlier this year, but has now been pushed back to 2027.

And based on further reporting from Kotaku, you may not want to get your hopes up too high for this one.

While the project is purportedly progressing and is poised to hit an “alpha” milestone soon, it’s allegedly over budget and has been scaled back significantly.

Curiously, journalist Rebekah Valentine reports that the title was originally intended for Netflix, but transitioned to consoles like PS5 during development.

As such, gameplay is said to be light, “primarily using only one button and lacking significant interaction”.

If you felt this year’s Marvel’s Wolverine was a bit basic, then it sounds like this may end up even more simplistic by comparison.

#4103. Mystic Messenger's most loyal players are getting banned in droves for seemingly playing the game too much

With the 10th anniversary of Mystic Messenger nearly upon us, the dating sim has inexplicably begun issuing wide-spread bans for its most active players.

Mystic Messenger, arguably one of the best dating sims around, has been dormant for about seven years. Despite not receiving new content or any meaningful updates in all that time, the game remains popular with its core fans, many of whom just woke up to some shocking news about their accounts.

The free-to-play mobile dating sim has started banning players with seemingly too many Hourglasses - the game’s virtual currency - saved up in their accounts. So far, it looks like players with 1,000 or more have been targeted, but others with far fewer hoards have reported getting the axe, too.

The news exploded on the Mystic Messenger subreddit overnight, with over a dozen reports from players logging in to play normally, only to receive an in-game notice that their accounts had been banned.

The message players received is identical, and doesn’t mention the specific reason for the ban. “Your account has been banned because abusive behavior has been detected from your account,” it reads, ending with a support email address the affected user can contact if they believe they’d banned in error.

It didn’t take a while for players to realise that most, if not all of the bans are for players with thousands of Hourglasses in their accounts. The virtual currency can both be acquired in-game just by playing, as well as through direct real-money purchases.

For a nearly ten-year-old game that stopped receiving content three years into its life, it’s easy to see how a dedicated group of players would be able to acquire so many Hourglasses by simply playing regularly for so long.

When contacted by the affected players, Cheritz, the developer and publisher of the game, has instructed them to send receipts of how they acquired Hourglasses (assuming they were purchased) to verify whether or not they’d been fraudulently obtained.

Considering that Mystic Messenger has practically been abandoned by its developer, certain exploits have emerged over the years that allowed players to farm Hourglasses faster than intended, but those instances have always been dealt with then and there.

The blanket and sudden nature of this ban is what’s spooked players, especially those who’ve been logging in for years and never thought accruing in-game currency from playing the game too much would make them the target of a ban.

The running theory is that most of the bans are unintentional, and may be the result of a new automated security system that’s been implemented. It’s entirely possible, especially if its’s AI-based, that the new system simply couldn’t distinguish between those who have earned (or bought) their Hourglasses fairly, and those who used exploits.

The timing of the ban wave is also suspect. With the game’s 10th anniversary coming up in July, it could be that Cheriz is preparing to release a large update for Mystic Messenger, which may include new content. If most of the playerbase is already sitting on massive amounts of in-game currency, they may simply use that to fast-track their way to unlocking the new content, which would greatly affect the developer’s bottom line.

This is a problem that other live service games have run into in the past. Just recently, extraction shooter Arc Raiders added a cap to the amount of Cred players can hold in their accounts very quickly after its launch. That currency is used to buy cosmetic sets in the store, so the logic is easy to follow.

All of that has certainly put a damper on the enthusiasm of the game’s most active players, many of whom were excited to get together in person for the coming 10th anniversary, participate in community nights and so on to celebrate.

It’s also disheartening to see a fanbase so loyal; playing a game as regularly for so long without new content, to be treated so poorly. Even without knowing what the game is, it’s impressive that so many people have kept the flag of their favourite game flying for so long.

A new GTA London probably isn't happening anytime soon

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Rockstar North co-studio head and GTA 6 lead Rob Nelson says that there's always a chance GTA could leave the United States, but there's still too much to do with America.

Grand Theft Auto – especially from the 3D era onwards – has pretty much always been a satire of American culture. The games are rife with excess, with billboards, radio ads, and in-game companies that couldn't be more exaggerated if they tried, with the entire series very much being an outsider's view of American culture tuned up to its capitalist extremes. GTA 4 in particular is very much a deconstruction of the concept of the "American Dream" with Niko Bellic leaving his sordid past behind to start a new life in New York only to discover the sensationalized vision of the states is far from the reality.

This in turn causes debate whenever the idea of setting a GTA game outside of the states emerges. Many see the American culture to be so ingrained into the DNA of the series that it simply wouldn't work without it. Speaking to The Guardian, Nelson was asked about the idea, with the developer responding, "Never say never, but there's still so much to do in America."

When asked if Rockstar's roots in Scotland, with a ton of its studios residing outside the US, gave the developer a unique take on the country, he explains, "I think we're all outsiders to this version of America," adding, "no one experiences the America that we're portraying here in its fullness."

Given it's been almost 20 years since GTA took place in New York, I can't imagine there will be a non-USA game in the series for a while yet, as presumably that would be next in line for the series. Plus there's always the chance the studio strays away from its trio of California, New York, and Florida for a new state next time around.

Also yes, I'm aware there were London-based expansions for the original GTA.

GTA 6 won't run at 60fps even on PS5 Pro, but Sony's console does have an exclusive: ray-traced shadows and PSSR.

#4101. Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang Resigns Following Infidelity Scandal

Company produces custom processor for Switch 2

Nvidia, one of the largest tech firms in the world and the company responsible for the Switch 2's custom processor, has found itself embroiled in scandal over recent days.

As reported by The Guardian, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang, who you might recognise from the 'Creator's Voice Special Edition' video for Switch 2, has now resigned after reported affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and a company employee.

He will be replaced on an interim basis by Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, until a full-time successor is named. Nvidia's share price began to sharply decline following reports of the scandal, to the point where it is now no longer the most valuable company in the world.

The BBC speculates that Huang's departure could set him up to be a "formidable opponent" to the very company he co-founded, with Elon Musk stating that it would be "an honour" to work with him at SpaceX.

With regards to Nintendo, it's likely that none of this will have any immediate impact on Nvidia's relationship with the Japanese company. Nvidia will no doubt be under contract to supply custom chips for the Switch 2, but what happens with the inevitable Switch 2 successor is under question.

Hopefully everything will go smoothly for Nintendo, but if it wants to utilise Nvidia's architecture for its next console – particularly for backwards compatibility – then its efforts may be impacted by Huang's departure along with Nvidia's sharp pivot towards AI.

Of course, it's really early to be speculating about the 'Switch 3', but you can bet that Nintendo's R&D department will be looking at all of this very closely and considering its potential impact.

#4100. Forza Horizon 6 explodes on Steam even before it's officially out

Forza Horizon 6 looks to have easily delivered the most successful launch for any game in the series on PC, with record-breaking player numbers.

Steam is abuzz this week with a couple of long-anticipated launches, but in Forza Horizon 6’s case, at least, the game isn’t even out for what will be most of its players. The anticipated sequel in the open-world driving game series doesn’t officially launch until May 19, but owners of its most expensive version - the Premium Edition - can play it right now.

That version of the game includes more than just a few days of early access, of course, but you’d think the $120 price tag would’ve only been palatable to a small group of players. Not the case with this game.

Forza Horizon 6, which has spent 16 weeks in Steam’s global top sellers list, currently occupies the number two spot, having jumped up three spots this week in anticipation of the launch. The game has also naturally been popular with players, so popular in fact that it has already overtaken the player counts of all other Horizon games on the platform.

At the time of writing, the game has peaked at 128,157 concurrent players on Steam alone (via SteamDB). The figure has already climbed several times during the writing of this story, so you can only imagine how much higher it’s going to get deeper into the weekend.

All of that, of course, days before the official launch on Tuesday, when, theoretically, the majority of the game’s audience will be able to start playing. In just a few short hours, Horizon 6 has already gone well above Forza Horizon 5’s peak concurrent of 81,096, as well as Forza Horizon 4’s peak 75,689 players.

Steam is the only platform that publishes player numbers, of course, but it’s easy to see how similar the enthusiasm is going to be on Xbox. Though the game is not yet part of the Game Pass line-up, those who don’t want to wait could buy the Premium Edition Upgrade to get the included content, and play it right now.

Game Pass, and Xbox / Windows Store numbers don’t factor into Steam’s, which is another thing to consider when viewing the numbers holistically. Indeed, given how successful Forza Horizon 5 has been on PlayStation 5, Horizon 6’s upcoming release on Sony's console is bound to be even bigger.

Forza Horizon 5 has been off to a similarly flying start in the first few days of its own advanced access launch, so it’s obviously not surprising to see Horizon 6 do better there. In case you missed it, check out our review of Forza Horizon 6. In short, we really liked it, even if we expected more.

#4098. Guide: PlayStation Studios: All Sony First-Party Developers and What They're Working On

Sony's first-party developers are known collectively as PlayStation Studios, and it's these teams that make all the games published by the company.

Whether it's PS5, PC, or beyond, there are always new games in the works. While we don't always know everything about what's in development, we've done our best to collate all the current info in this page.

Below, you'll find a list of every subsidiary studio under Sony's umbrella as well as what they're currently working on. We'll be updating this article every so often, when new information comes to light.

On this page: PlayStation Studios: All Sony First-Party Developers and What They're Working On

Here are all of Sony's teams working out of the company's home country.

Originally an internal development unit named Polys Entertainment, Polyphony Digital is best known for creating Sony’s flagship racing simulation franchise, Gran Turismo.

Current Projects: Polyphony has been supporting Gran Turismo 7 consistently since launch, with lots of free updates adding new events and vehicles. While this looks set to continue, we expect work has begun on the studio's next game, which will presumably be another Gran Turismo.

Team Asobi rose from the ashes of Japan Studio, initially an internal group building tech demos and on-boarding software such as The Playroom. It brought us Astro Bot Rescue Mission for PSVR, PS5 pack-in game Astro's Playroom, and is now best known for its full-fledged 3D platformer, Astro Bot.

Current Projects: Team Asobi's post-launch updates and support for Astro Bot appears to have concluded, so we can presume the whole studio is now working on its next game. It isn't known what that game is, though given Astro's success, we reckon a sequel is likely.

Below you'll find details on all of SIE's European studios.

Firesprite has an interesting history; it was initially formed by developers from Studio Liverpool, an old Sony studio shuttered in 2012. After The Persistence and supporting Sony on The Playroom and The Playroom VR, it made Horizon Call of the Mountain alongside Guerrilla. It's now SIE's largest UK-based studio.

Current Projects: Firesprite is currently working on Until Dawn 2, a narrative horror adventure game coming to PS5 in January 2027.

Creators of the Killzone franchise, and acquired by Sony following the release of Shellshock: ‘Nam 67 in 2005. One of SIE's most technically capable studios, it's now best known for Horizon Zero Dawn, which runs on the studio's own Decima Engine.

Current Projects: Guerrilla is currently making Horizon Hunters Gathering, a co-op action game with roguelike elements and a very different art style. Also in the works is Horizon Steel Frontiers, an MMO being built for PC and mobile; NCSOFT is spearheading production, but Guerrilla is involved as well. It can also be safely assumed that Horizon 3 is in the pipeline.

Finnish developer Housemarque has worked closely with Sony for over a decade. The studio specialises in arcade-like action, bringing us titles such as Super Stardust HD, Resogun, and of course its latest work, Returnal. The success of the latter pushed Sony to acquire the team in 2021.

Current Projects: Housemarque recently released Saros, a rogue-lite third-person action game that builds on the Returnal formula. It has since released a free update adding more content and features. Plans for what comes next are unknown.

The makers of the LittleBigPlanet franchise, and one of Sony’s most imaginative studios. Media Molecule was acquired by Sony in 2010 following the success of Sackboy’s inaugural adventure.

Current Projects: With post-launch support of Dreams now concluded, Media Molecule is working on its next project, which will be a new IP. It's expected this will reduce the focus on creation and will be a more traditional game. Reports suggest it's making an Animal Crossing-esque life sim.

A company held aloft for its uniformly excellent PC ports, Sony acquired Nixxes in 2021 for this exact purpose. It's mostly been focused on porting existing PlayStation Studios titles to PC, but made its first real creative effort with Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered in 2024.

Current Projects: Nixxes collaborated with Housemarque on Saros. It's also likely to be working on unannounced PC ports.

XDEV is a team that mostly concerns itself with providing support to external teams that are making PlayStation-exclusive titles. Over the years it has helped bring many games to PS5 and PS4, such as Detroit: Become Human, Returnal, Death Stranding, Stellar Blade, Rise of the Ronin, and many others. Though it originated in the UK, the company now also operates in the US and Japan.

Current Projects: XDEV is working with Housemarque on Saros, Arc System Works on Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls, and presumably more yet to be announced.

Most of Sony's best-known studios hail from the United States. Here they all are — plus a bonus Canada team!

Infamously created Bubsy 3D for the PS1 before moving on to the Syphon Filter series under the Eidetic name. Acquired by Sony in 2000. Historically focused on portable games, the team broke back into AAA territory with Days Gone on PS4.

Current Projects: Unknown, though reportedly it won't be a Days Gone sequel.

Famed for its expertise in first-person shooters, Bungie has made some of gaming's best-loved franchises in Halo and Destiny. Thanks to its work on the latter, Sony acquired the company in 2022 during its big push into multiplayer and live service games. Bungie has retained some autonomy under this new ownership, though this has softened over time.

Current Projects: Bungie's latest is Marathon, a reinvention of its own sci-fi shooter series from the 90s. This iteration is an intense extraction shooter that launched in March 2026. It'll be supporting this game for the foreseeable future.

A new studio co-founded by Jade Raymond, famed for her work on the Assassin's Creed and Watch Dogs series. The developer has yet to release a game, but has been scooped up by Sony as the team works on its debut project.

Current Projects: Haven was developing the now-cancelled Fairgames, an online multiplayer shooter described as a "competitive heist experience". The studio is currently acting in a support role for other teams.

Famed for PlayStation exclusive series such as Ratchet & Clank and Resistance, the developer has felt like part of the first party family all along. With Marvel's Spider-Man and Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales being such huge hits, it's no wonder Sony scooped the studio up in 2019.

Current Projects: Insomniac recently released Marvel's Wolverine exclusively for PS5 in September 2026. It's extremely likely that Marvel's Spider-Man 3 is in the works, too.

Perhaps the most famous of Sony’s studios, Naughty Dog has a long history creating series such as Crash Bandicoot, Jak & Daxter, Uncharted, and The Last of Us. Acquired in 2001.

Current Projects: Naughty Dog is currently working on sci-fi action adventure game Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet. It's expected this will launch in 2027, though no release information has been announced yet.

Most famous for the critically acclaimed MLB The Show series, San Diego Studio has previously operated as a support studio for external developers, and has also worked on titles like The Mark of Kri and Pain.

Current Projects: San Diego Studio recently launched MLB The Show 26, the latest instalment in its annual series. It's also working on MLB The Show Mobile.

Creators of the God of War franchise. Previously incubated developers like thatgamecompany, while also serving as a support studio for external developers working on exclusive games.

Current Projects: Santa Monica Studio's next game is God of War Laufey, a game following Faye and what happens to her after she dies at the start of God of War (2018). This is due for release in May 2027. Additionally, the team has announced God of War Trilogy Remake, which revisits the Greek mythology games, though this is further out.

One-time Nintendo 64 developer, Sucker Punch is the creator of PlayStation fan favourites like Sly Cooper and inFAMOUS. Acquired by Sony in 2011, the studio is now best known for Ghost of Tsushima.

Current Projects: Sucker Punch most recently released Ghost of Yotei, an indirect sequel to Ghost of Tsushima. Ghost of Yotei Legends, a co-op multiplayer DLC, is now also available. It's unknown what the studio's next game will be.

One of Sony's newest studios, teamLFG is a developer that began as a standalone team within Bungie, but has now spun out to become its own thing. It has yet to release a game.

Current Projects: teamLFG is working on something currently known as Project Gummybears. It's described as a "team-based action game that draws inspiration from fighting games, platformers, MOBAs, life sims, and frog-type games" set within a "lighthearted" and "comedic" sci-fi universe.

Valkyrie is perhaps best known for its GUNS UP! series, which Sony published on various platforms prior to the acquisition. After being a reliable external collaborator on several projects, Valkyrie Entertainment was brought into PlayStation Studios in December 2021. It has since provided support on numerous games including God of War Ragnarok, The Last of Us Part II Remastered, and Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection.

Current Projects: Valkyrie Entertainment holds its cards very close to its chest, so it's difficult to know what it's working on. It can be assumed it's helping out across various projects within PlayStation Studios.

That's everything we know about PlayStation Studios and its current projects. Which is your favourite of Sony's first-party developers? What games do you want to see them make next? Discuss in the comments section below.

As the Editor of Push Square, Sammy has over 15 years of experience analysing the world of PlayStation, from PS3 through PS5 and everything in between. He’s an expert on PS Studios and industry matters, as well as sports games and simulators. He also enjoys RPGs when he has the time to dedicate to them, and is a bit of a gacha whale.

If I had to rank the top five Sony developers in terms of what I’ve seen in terms of fun, graphically and/or technologically impressive games along with potential for future awesomeness:

1. Naughty Dog. It’s been the juggernaut, top dog, tour de force studio that Microsoft’s always dreamt of having, and it’s what Rare should’ve/would’ve been if MS hadn’t wasted Rare’s time with avatars and Kinect experiences.

2. Insomniac. Ratchet and Clank. Spiderman. Spyro. Yeah, Insomniac rules. Here’s hoping for a Feral Rights sequel/remake for PSVR 2, done with the size, scope, and budget a true AAA game should have! Make the system seller VR2 truly needs and deserves. Put our faith back into VR, Sony (or send the job over to MediaMolecule because they’re known for their innovative tech-based PlayStation games.

3. Santa Monica Studios. God of War. Boom!

4. Sucker Punch. InFAMOUS 2 was so, so good! After years of trying different open world games, InFAMOUS 2 was the first one that I truly sunk my teeth into. It was my personal gateway to an entirely new gaming world. And the ability within that game to create and design your own missions? Revolutionary! SP took a slight step back with InFAMOUS: Second Son and First Light, but their work in creating Sly Cooper keeps them at #3.

4. Housemarque. Fantastic action games. In an alternate universe where arcades still exist, Housemarque would be #1 and it wouldn’t even be close.

5. Guerrilla Games. Killzone. Horizon. Awesome-sauce.

As an aside, I love ClapHanz for the fantastic Hot Shots Golf games (which includes the VR game, too!). It’s a pity Sony didn’t pony up the bucks to buy the studio. I’d have loved to see more Hot Shots entries in golf and other sports—tennis, baseball, football, basketball, soccer, volleyball, fencing, curling, hockey, tee-ball, tag, axe throwing, log cutting, fencing, corn detasseling—heck, it doesn’t matter what sports are represented. If it’s done by ClapHanz, it’s good.

@Oram77 Yeah, I didn’t intend to cast any blame or criticism, per se, rather more of a surprising (and disappointing) observation. It is what it is. Development takes ages now. Added to that the poor strategic planning that resulted in several cancelled projects and studio closures and… here we are.

I don’t hold it against Bluepoint or Media Molecule necessarily. It’s just crazy to think they might go the length of the entire generation without a release (Demon’s Souls Remake at launch notwithstanding). I’m sure BluePoint’s PS6 game will be fantastic. And I suspect Mm will squeeze out something on PS5, and it will probably be good too.

The development cycles for even studios that didn’t have years wasted on a canceled project are now around 5-6 years (Taking Ghost of Yotei as an example. Or Death Stranding 2) whereas it was previously about 2 years, especially for sequels. (Again using Sucker Punch as an example — Infamous 2009, Infamous 2 2011, Infamous: Festival of Blood 2011, Infamous Second Son 2014, Infamous First Light 2014.)

I’m not saying anything we don’t already know, development times have increased 2-4x compared to prior generations. It’s one reason why AI may not be such a bad thing as a tool to streamline some of the tasks of development, so long as it doesn’t replace the creative parts of the process. If it can improve efficiency and keep production on track (and keep a studio from being shut down as a result) then maybe that’s a good thing. But that’s a whole other discussion for debate.

I will say also, that despite the drastic ballooning of game development times, there has been an equally significant expansion in number of developers producing games, particularly from emerging markets. As a result there is no shortage of games to play and in fact, we have more games than ever before to choose from. So I don’t necessarily want to imply that it’s doom and gloom.

#4097. Honkai: Star Rail Version 4.3 will take us deeper into the World in Canvas and make Mortenax Blade playable

Honkai: Star Rail's next big outing will see the continuation of the Planarcadia story, and it's going to be with us soon.

HoYoverse has today delivered full details on the next major update for Honkai: Star Rail. Version 4.3, dubbed The Lethe Below the Living, will be available for all players on June 1. The upcoming update adds a new chapter to the Planarcadia arc, and introduce a new playable character.

The new narrative chapter will also unveil more about Mortenax Blade, the Trailblazer themselves, and the husk of the Aeon.

Mortenax Blade is the hero of this chapter, and he’s going to step into the World in Canvas. The goal is to - by borrowing the power of Voracity - excise Shuhu from his body and end the curse.

The Trailblazer goes on a trip of their own in Version 4.3, this time to Inkford Hermitage, right on the edge between the World in Canvas and the real world. They’re going to undertake this journey to warn Graphia of the Asat Pramad threat.

In case you hadn’t already guessed, Mortenax Blade is this version’s new playable character. The 5-Star Fire-Type swordsman is on the Path of Nihility. Blade’s Ultimate allows him to enter an enhanced state by deploying a special Bounded Field.

While the field is active, all enemies receive more DMG. Entering this state is also how Blade unlocks his skill, which uses a Sword Formation to deal more damage. This is then used to essentially unlock a second, more powerful Ultimate for him.

The benefits of Mortenax Blade’s kit extend to his teammates, too. Any ally who attacks an enemy with him on the team, they inflict a debuff on them. This also builds up a special Charge that Blade can later use with his Skill.

Version 4.3’s launch arrives alongside the Gift of Tempered Blade event. Through it, you can claim a new Trailblazer Outfit piece for free, but only after getting Mortenax Blade from Warping. The first phase’s rerun will be Yao Guang, and the second phase will bring back both Cyrene and Phainon.

You can also expect the Wispae Amusement Park to arrive within the World in Canvas, which you’ll get to design. You can plan where the rides will go, pick the different themes, set visitor routes and more.

Starward Mode is another new addition, which can be found in Memory of Chaos, Pure Fiction, and Apocalyptic Shadow. Starward will see you take on three different stages, which you’ll need three teams for. Clearing each challenge with full stars will reward you 100 Stellar Jades extra per chase.

There’s more coming down the line, too. A new Fate/Stay Night [Unlimited Blade Works] collaboration will arrive in a content up this summer. The event will give players a chance to earn Gilgamesh or Archer for free by logging in.

#4096. GTA 6 Gets 20 Seconds Of New Gameplay, And Everyone Can't Believe How Real It Looks

Here's a bit more footage that has also just appeared today:

Original Story: Sorry to keep bombarding you with GTA 6 hype, but we're literally one week away from the biggest video game launch of all time, and even 20 seconds' worth of gameplay is getting millions of views ahead of November 19th's launch.

This latest footage comes from a weird source - an Instagram account called "Only in Dade". The gameplay shows someone cruising down the road and looking at supercars out the window, while a mass of NPCs are also shown either admiring the vehicles or just making their way down the street.

Here's the footage (we can't embed the original, so you'll find the Reddit repost below):

This is clearly a marketing stunt and not necessarily representative of what you'll be seeing in the game, but it does appear to be real GTA 6 footage - Rockstar Games was spotted sharing and liking the video shortly after it went live.

It also appears to be a take on a similar real-life video from Miami that was taken last month:

Our best look at gameplay for GTA 6 to date has still been the Extended Preview from back in August, which certainly gives us a better idea of what to expect than 20 seconds' worth of gameplay.

We'll take anything we can get at this point though, and it's making the wait even harder for November 19th!

#4095. Professor Layton And The New World Of Steam English Voice Cast Revealed

It has been a tense wait to see whether Level-5 would bring in real, human voice actors for the regional dubs of Professor Layton and The New World of Steam, or whether it would slip into the ol' AI that its CEO seems to bring up at every given opportunity. Fortunately, it's positive news.

The dev has today revealed the game's English voice cast, and it's headed up by Christopher Robin Miller and Lani Minella — the returning North American Layton and Luke voice actors from the main series. You can even hear a snippet of them in action on the game's website, and yes, the nostalgia is a welcome listen.

The returning actors will be joined by the likes of Amber Lee Connors (Persona 4 Revival, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, Unicorn Overlord), Nic Olsen (Genshin Impact), Arthur Romeo (Street Fighter 6, AI: The Somnium Files - nirvanA Initiative) and more.

Interestingly, Cat Protano (Xenoblade Chronicles X: Definitive Edition, Trails in the Sky) seems to be taking on the role of Luke in the UK dub, and not the previous main series actor, Maria Darling.

The website also showcases the cast list for the game's French, Italian, German and Spanish dubs, all of which use real voice actors — what a concept!

Pre-orders for the New World of Steam's PC and PS5 releases have gone live today, with Switch 1 and 2 pre-orders expected at a later date.

It's worth pointing out that the newly published Steam page doesn't feature the site's AI disclosure, which is required for all games that use visual or other in-game AI assets. The lack of a disclosure doesn't mean AI hasn't been used under the hood (CEO Akihiro Hino said it hasn't been used anywhere in the game), but the last few years following Level-5 have made us cautious at every turn.

Years after its initial reveal, Professor Layton and the New World of Steam finally got a firm release date back in the September Direct: 10th December. We're cautious about getting our expectations too high around it, but the returning voice cast goes a long way toward alleviating some initial fears.

#4094. Monopoly Go x The Simpsons crossover is almost here

After a long wait and exhaustive leaks, the highly-anticipated Simpsons event will finally arrive in Monopoly Go very soon, alongside new content.

Monopoly Go players have been looking forward to a major crossover event for what felt like months, and though most of the details ended up leaking, nothing actually beats official information.

The world of The Simpsons has officially arrived in Monopoly Go, and there's a whole lot for players to dive into. The show's creative team even produced a new animated short, featuring Mr. Monopoly, and Mr. Burns.

Available June 3 through July 29, the new event allows Monopoly Go players to jump in the world of The Simpsons. You'll be able to build, and explore all around multiple iconic locations from the show.

Along the way, you'll run into Simpsons characters like Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa, and of course, Mr. Burns. Developer Scopely teamed up with the show's creative team to create many references, and Easter Eggs for you to discover. You'll find some of those on chance cards, but most of the world has been changed to be part of The Simpsons, including getting to bribe Chief Wiggum to escape jail.

The developer promises a deeply connected world with Simpsons narratives and characters that alter seasonal maps, and offer unique sticker sets and animated sequences to dive in. Incidentally, this is The Simpsons' first appearance in a mobile-exclusive game in 13 years.

Here's a breakdown of everything you can expect, straight from Scopely:

Episodes: Narrative-driven encounters that create stories inspired by The Simpsons. Episodes play out across seasonal boards, sticker sets, and minigames, all capped off with an animated short.

Sticker sets: Every Episode comes with its own limited-time sticker set, taking cues from the latest Simpsons story. Collectible artwork, character journeys and other rewards are yours to claim for the duration of each Episode.

The Simpsons Run: Every two weeks, a new Springfield character will take over the Free Parking tile, kicking off character-driven runs.

Simpsons-themed Shutdowns and Heists: Monopoly Go's shutdowns and heists get a Simpsons makeover, with Springfield-inspired chaos and disasters.

Bribe Wiggum: This changes Go to Jail to allow players to bribe Chief Wiggum, giving you a chance to earn a bigger reward, but not without introducing an element of unpredictability.

Simpsons chance cards: The chance card collection grows with over 50 Simpsons-themed cards full of memes, references and one-liners from the show.

If you're excited to jump in tomorrow, be sure to check out these Free Monopoly Go Dice Links before you dive into the new content.

It's now alleged that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia employee

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

It hasn't been a great week for Nvidia. After CEO Jensen Huang was alleged to be having an affair with a suspected Chinese spy, reports have now emerged with allegations of a second affair – this time with an Nvidia employee – and now the company's board is reportedly considering ousting its leader.

Huang issued a statement earlier this week admitting to an affair, saying, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry." He also acknowledged the concerns that the person he cheated on his wife with could be a spy, saying: "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American."

However, per new reports, the situation may be even more complex than it first appeared. The New York Times claims that, according to five anonymous individuals who worked at Nvidia, Huang also had an affair with an executive at the company – vice president of healthcare Kimberly Powell. It's alleged that the pair's relationship had been discussed internally at Nvidia, and that they'd been seen being affectionate with each other during a conference in March. What's more, one bystander allegedly filmed this interaction, but was asked to sign a nondisclosure agreement.

Huang has not acknowledged these latest accusations – the NYT says that when it called him yesterday, he said, "I don’t think you should be talking to me directly," and promptly ended the call.

But it doesn't end there. The Wall Street Journal claims (via BBC News) that Nvidia's board is meeting to decide Huang's future at the company – basically, whether or not to oust him. The BBC reports that Huang's first affair had been something that, in tech circles, was seen as something that could be moved on from, but the alleged second one could prove more problematic as far as the board is concerned – particularly since it apparently involves an employee (who NYT claims reports to him). A tech insider told the BBC, succinctly, "He's cooked."

Huang has been the CEO of Nvidia since its inception 33 years ago, so any change here would be unprecedented for the company.

Nvidia GeForce RTX 60-series graphics cards could be sidelined until 2028, making it the longest gap between GPU generations in 20 years.

#4091. Intergalactic PS5 in the 'Last Stage of Production', Gameplay Coming Next Year

Neil Druckmann thinks the game will "surprise people"

Since the announcement of Naughty Dog's next big game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, we really haven't seen or heard much about it. In 2027, though, that's set to change.

In a brief appearance on a live show at Comic Creators Block Party 2026, director Neil Druckmann has teased a few things about the upcoming sci-fi adventure.

You can see all the Intergalactic chatter in the post below:

Druckmann says the game is at the "last stage of production", meaning "we can play it, we're refining and polishing it". He says he "can't wait to show it to the world."

It sounds like 2027 will be big for Intergalactic, as Sony and Naughty Dog will "show a lot of it next year" including "gameplay" and "more of the story". Whether the game actually launches next year is another question, but at the very least we'll be seeing plenty more of it.

"I think it'll really surprise people, what they think the game is and what it actually is," Druckmann says.

He also talks about how Naughty Dog has been making "relatively grounded" games for a long time with Uncharted and The Last of Us, and Intergalactic presents an opportunity for the team to explore something more fantastical.

"Something we've been really hungry for is to go sci-fi," he says, referring to the studio's previous series, Jak & Daxter.

"We really wanted to take everything we learned from that franchise, which is sci-fi/fantasy, the pulp action adventure stuff we learned with Uncharted, the more serious drama we got from The Last of Us... [Intergalactic] really is a combination of those three franchises."

Druckmann continues, talking about how the aim is to combine Naughty Dog's cinematic storytelling chops with "deeper gameplay systems" in Intergalactic.

I'm super excited to finally learn more about this game in 2027; fingers crossed its release won't be too far behind.

@GirlVersusGame So true — depending on the game there can be some importance to relatability to the character you play as, but usually that’s not limited by the protagonist’s gender or orientation, in my experience. I loved playing as (and could relate to) Aloy, Lara Croft, Jesse, Max Caulfield, Selene (Returnal), Kay Vess (SW Outlaws), Amicia (Plague Tale), or Kat, as well as playing as Kratos, Nathan Drake, Miles Morales, Cal Kestis (SW Jedi games), Snake, Joel, or Sam Bridges. Part of gaming is experiencing a fictional world and doing things you can’t do in real life. Sometimes being able to relate to the character adds some extra value, but also sometimes role playing as someone different from you also adds to the impact of the experience. I also feel that games can be a great way to learn and broaden one’s horizons. I think there’s just a general lack of open-mindedness that a sector of the fandom lack. And that’s all fine, people can play or not play according to their heart’s desire but in the case of many games, I think they do themselves a disservice by ruling out a game simply because of the outward appearance of a character or a perception of the traits of the character. I guess it’s summed in the old adage ‘don’t judge a book by its cover.’
