We're probably still a ways out from playing Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, but Naughty Dog's given us a little tease about what to expect. According to studio head Neill Druckmann, it's an amalgamation of many of the company's biggest series thus far, which sounds rather exciting.

"We used to have another game franchise called Jak and Daxter," he said on Comic Creators Block Party 2026 with Patton Oswalt. "And with this one, we really wanted to take everything we learned from that franchise, which is sci-fi fantasy, the action-adventure stuff we learned with Uncharted, the more kind of serious drama we got for The Last of Us, and it really is a combination of those three franchises."

He goes on to mention that the team wanted to test themselves on what they could accomplish mechanically. "We wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems," Druckmann explains. "Can we sustain the cinematic storytelling we're used to doing and go even deeper with gameplay systems?"

Honestly, referencing Jak and Daxter is enough to pique my interest. That series of mythical platformers wound up sidelined once the Uncharted games started taking off, leading us to The Last of Us. Much as I enjoy battling the Cordyceps, I miss the bounciness of Jak and Daxter, and I hope this means Intergalactic won't be quite so self-serious.

Druckmann mentions Naughty Dog is heading into the "last stages of production" with Intergalactic right now. "We can play it, and we're refining and polishing it," he says. We've seen remarkably little of the project since the reveal trailer at The Game Awards 2024, and that only really introduced the main character, Jordan A Mun, and made it clear we're in the far future.

His candor may suggest another trailer is on the horizon. It being Naughty Dog, I won't hold my breath, but it seems like this is a game that'll appeal to fans of almost every era of the company. No bad thing when you have that team's track record.

The Last of Us directors used to say "nobody" was making "character-driven survival action games" like them – just don't tell that to Resident Evil

#4087. Dune: Awakening's seasonally appropriate Blood and Ice expansion gets a December release date, and in a plus for preservation, an offline mode this month

December is certainly going to be the month of Dune. The biggest Dune of Dunecember will obviously go to Dune: Part 3, which is Duen out December 18th. A little bit before that, however, is a well-timed free expansion coming to Dune: Awakening. It's called Blood and Ice, which sounds gross, but hey, I guess free blood and ice isn't entirely a bad thing?

"The expansion introduces the Polar Sink, an entirely new survival map where everything you've learned about surviving in the desert will be put to the test," explains a Steam blog post. "Instead of protecting yourself from extreme heat, you'll need to find ways to stay warm. The technology you've developed to survive the desert won't be enough here, and you'll need to upgrade your equipment, gather new resources, and adapt your strategies to survive the cold."

You'll find two biomes in the Polar Sink, the tundra and the ice cap, the former being where you'll kick off your time in this expansion. "While conditions here are more manageable than on the ice cap itself, these families won't welcome anyone interfering with their operations," the blog notes. Your main goal is to get the ice cap and gather up all of its valuable resources, namely, ice! Said ice can then be used to "cool your base equipment and speed up production."

Apparently you'll get about 35 more hours of "new progression, along with new vehicle modules, augments, and specialization traits," out of the expansion, and there are plans for future updates that'll give you reason to come back to the Polar Sink in Duen time. Beyond that, there is also a new cosmetic store, which lets you purchase "optional cosmetic items, including outfits, vehicle variants, and additional ways to customize your bases." I'm sure this will go down well.

Perhaps most importantly, this November will see the arrival of offline mode, meaning you don't need an internet connection to play it. Hopefully if (probably when (sorry to be a pessimist (realist))) the servers go down, this means it'll still be playable. Character copying so that you can copy your character from multiplayer servers to single-player will be coming in January, alongside full cross-play. Lots coming essentially!

#4086. Gag Order is a co-op, SCP-ish horror shooter about surviving as best you can against some nasty, tentacle covered cephalopod creatures

Don't let it touch me, please and thank you

What makes Carrion interesting obviously lies in playing as the monster in a horror game rather than being the one chased down by it. The game's nasty tentacle monster still gives me the heebie jeebies, so I really would hate to be hunted by one. This is where I point you towards Gag Order, a shooter where you are in fact hunted by a disgusting cephalopod creature all while tracking down a distress signal.

Gag Order is not designed to be played solo, it feels wrong to call it friendslop given how unfriendly it is in vibes, but it does feel like it fits into a similar lineage as Lethal Company at the very least. In it, you are a research lab's Guardian Unit member, and you get a distress call "from one of the core parts of the complex." Upon arrival, the atmosphere is rotten, and you quickly come to understand that you are not equipped for what you have to deal with.

The solution, then, is to take care of those nightmare-inducing cephalopod creatures. Except during the first phase of a run, it sounds like they're invincible. Your guns do seem to be able to fend them off at the very least, but it's the second phase, which is geared around a "fast paced team-bossight" where it sounds like you'll be trying to take these things down. I'm not quite sure what the process is to get between those two phases, but I'm quite fond of the vibes on display.

It feels a touch reminiscent of 2000s shooters with some slightly contemporary mechanical sensibilities. I'm fond of the light SCP vibes it has going on, alongside the faint surrealness of certain elements like a bunch of crows hanging out in an abandoned office building. Creepy! Good looking stuff. Gag Order is apparently due out by the end of 2026, though we're obviously getting close there, so it's worth keeping an eye on it by throwing it a wishlist on Steam, if it takes your fancy.

Walmart Collectibles DrawAlthough you aren't guaranteed an item, you've got a chance of securing some must-have goodies at a much more reasonable cost if you get lucky. Here are the basic steps:- Set up a Walmart account with delivery address and default payment method.- Enter during the drawing window (Nov 12, 2:00pm - 3:00pm PST)- Wait for the results, because those who are selected get their order automatically placed. You then have six hours after the order to cancel or change your mind.

While the likes of the Pokemon Night Ultra Premium Collection are eye-catching (I've seen that going for double the price when looking where to buy Pokemon TCG 30th Celebration), I think the most notable items are actually the cheaper ones. Being able to pick up a Pokemon 30th Celebration Poster Collection for $19.97 is practically unheard of these days, for example.

In much the same way, it's so rare to see NeeDoh of any kind - but particularly the sought-after ones - available for $5 or thereabouts. If you wanted to grab the viral sensation, now's your chance.

Again, there's no guarantee of getting any of these... but a shot is better than none at all. And because no payment will be taken unless you actually get selected, you aren't losing anything either. Basically, you may as well give it a try and see what happens.

#4083. New Witcher 3 DLC Uses AI to Touch Up Geralt's Polish Voice Due to Actor's Health Issues

CD Projekt Red has worked with an AI voice generation company on next year's The Witcher 3 expansion, Songs of the Past, so the Polish voiceover for Geralt can match the original game.

Jacek Rozenek, the original Polish voice actor for Geralt has returned to voice the character for all the content in Songs of the Past. However, the actor unfortunately suffered a stroke in recent years that impacted his voice. This has left his voice unrecognisable compared to the lines he recorded for the original RPG.

Having received Rozenek's blessing, CD Projekt Red recorded all his voice work for Songs of the Past, and has taken that work to AI company Respeecher, who will make it sound like Geralt from the base game.

Again, this only affects the Polish language option. Doug Cockle has returned to voice Geralt for the English language version.

Rozenek suffered a stroke in 2019, and he was unable to speak following it. Through hours of training every day, he was able to return to voice acting in 2022, when CD Projekt Red released the PS5 version of The Witcher 3. There was a new quest in that edition, and the work he had to put into the voice lines accompanying it left Rozenek "exhausted" after the recording.

Rozenek has recorded his Polish voice lines for Songs of the Past as usual, but he's supportive of the developer's decision to involve Respeecher to make them sound like Geralt: "The point is that this voice should be as close as possible to my voice from 12 years ago. I have great trust... for the creators of this game."

Respeecher has used AI tools trained on Rozenek's previous work as Geralt to match the voices as much as possible.

News Here's 13 Minutes of Witcher 3: Songs of the Past DLC Gameplay

"We basically delivered to Respeecher all the lines that Jacek recorded for us for The Witcher 3,” explained localisation producer Mikołaj Szwed. “They created an algorithm of his voice, based on his lines."

Szwed added that CD Projekt Red only considered this route because of Rozenek's health issues, and having gained his blessing, thinks this is an "ethical" use of AI that can do some good.

Songs of the Past is slated to launch for PS5 at some point in 2027, off the back of the recently released The Witcher 3 Remastered.

[source gamefile.news, via videogameschronicle.com]

Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.

Personally, I see no issue with this whatsoever. It saves having someone attempting to impersonate the original Geralt voice, which if slightly different would have been somewhat jarring.

Also, I wish Rozenek's well with his health issues...

Must be just awful to have a stroke, one of the health issues that genuinely scares me, with a really hard recovery too. Poor chap, good to hear he's over the worst.

Nice to hear AI being used in a productive way for a change.

#4082. As if the injury descriptions weren't already ghastly enough in Dwarf Fortress, the legendary outpost builder is getting a "meat biome"

"Lots of meat terrain - muscle, bone, vertebral walls, sinew, sphincters."

Legendary outpost builder Dwarf Fortress is getting a meat biome. A terrible netherworld of bone and artery. A sunken redoubt of gristle and gizzard. An appalling labyrinth of squirt and squelch. Honestly, the biggest shock here is that Dwarf Fortress doesn't appear to have a meat biome already. It certainly has plenty of florid descriptions of fatal injuries.

These foul omens arrive care of a massive "Future of the Fortress" thread on the Bay 12 forums, in which studio co-founder (and prominent genAI disliker) Tarn "Toady One" Adams fields questions about the on-going development. As a forum thread, it's not a formal news source, so please season these tales of gutsy geology with whatever Condiment of Scepticism you consider appropriate.

There's no date for when the new biome might arrive, but Adams says it'll likely exist underground, and will be revolting. "Lots of meat terrain - muscle, bone, vertebral walls, sinew, sphincters," he promised. "We would have rivers of blood/fluids if we ever get to the fluid update, but no new fluids as it stands. We had thrown out the idea for maple syrup style taps on the vertebral walls for cosmic spinal fluid but alas, this is not in the game." At the very least, there won't be any meat trees, but you can mine the meat for resources.

Adams doesn't discuss the origins of the meat biome in the thread – is it more of a headless, fungal phenomenon, or is there some kind of huge mammalian cadaver down there? If it's the latter, one consolation is that the meat biome can't be resurrected. "Ha ha, I don't think regular meat can be animated currently?" Adams remarked in response to a question about biomes of squirming, zombified meat. "So probably not."

The bulk of the conversation around Dwarf Fortress at present concerns forthcoming changes to the magic system, together with how arcane knowledge is categorised, transmitted, preserved and lost throughout each procedurally generated world. There's a lot of speculative chat about that in the Future of the Fortress thread, too much to cleanly summarise. It's saying something about the density and stature of Dwarf Fortress that the addition of flesh caves feels like an afterthought.

Developer Bay 12's current plans for the game also include a crystal biome, which I would say is the nicer option, but then I remembered that this is Dwarf Fortress, the game in which you might end up getting besieged by the ghosts of the very children you callously sent to hunt down a wild elephant. There is absolutely going to be something in the crystal biome that gives you nightmares. Dazzling, prismatic nightmares.

#4080. Bond director Denis Villeneuve says he takes the responsibility of bringing the next 007 to the screen "very seriously"

Denis Villeneuve has no intention of getting Bond wrong

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

While we wait to find out the identity of the next James Bond, director Denis Villeneuve has touched on the responsibility of bringing 007 back to the screen for a new era. And he says, in no uncertain terms, "We can't f*** it up."

Speaking to GQ, Villeneuve was asked when filming begins on the 26th official Bond movie. And while he understandably deflected that question given they haven't even cast a Bond yet, Villeneuve did go on to talk about how seriously he takes the responsibility of his position.

"All the crew on Bond takes that responsibility very seriously, and we know that we cannot make mistake[s]. I was about to [say] we can't fuck it up. The truth is, we do not have the choice. We have to succeed. We have to honor the legacy, we have to honor the tradition, and there's a ton of Bond fans out there – I'm one of them – and I want this movie to be good, and I will work very hard to make sure we honor that responsibility."

Villeneuve sounds dead serious in the clip above, and given his track record in the last 10+ years, it's difficult to imagine a better person for the job. As for the all-important casting decision, all Villeneuve had to say was that it's "in the process" and "we are pushing the gas," but reports suggest there could be an official announcement before the end of the month, so it's possible a decision has already been made.

There are seemingly five finalists for the most coveted job in movies, with Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O'Connor among them. Late last week, it was revealed that Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult have also screen-tested, so whoever wins out will have triumphed over stiff competition.

As for Villeneuve, in little over a month the third and final instalment in his Dune trilogy hits screens with the release of Dune 3. While reviews aren't out yet, Paul Atreides star Timothée Chalamet has said he's "absolutely satisfied" with the movie's ending, telling The New York Times, "It didn't feel like the bar dropped at all." Bond hopeful and Dune 3 co-star Robert Pattinson also revealed a mind-blowing fact: there was a "350-foot-long model of a sandworm" on set.

Bond 26 does not currently have a release date. For more, check out our guide to all the most exciting upcoming movies heading your way this year and beyond.

#4079. Skyblivion modders reveal a former volunteer is "threatening to sue for damages upwards of €30,000" over work on the unofficial Oblivion remake project

"I just hope that we can get this resolved as soon as possible and get on with the planned release"

The team behind Oblivion remake mod Skyblivion are being threatened with legal action by a former volunteer on the project, according a video posted by current lead Kyle 'Rebelzize' Rebel. The situation looks like it'll need resolving before the mod, which was originally set to release last year, can finally make its way out of the Imperial City sewers.

"Recently, a former volunteer who contributed to Skyblivion’s development departed the project," the Skyblivion team outlined in a written statement and a YouTube video presented by Rebel. "We want to be completely transparent with the community about what has happened since their departure. After they left the project, we had several discussions regarding the continued use and maintenance of his work. The main disagreement centered on their objection to our decompilation of parts of their work — a necessary step our team took to maintain functionality and fix issues in systems already built into the project after access to the original source code repository was revoked."

"To protect ourselves from more stress and try and ensure a clean break, we decided to take the high road," Rebel explained in the video. "We have removed that work entirely. Thankfully due to some of our volunteers stepping up and simply learning new skill sets, as well as help from prominent Skyrim modders and permissions to use and integrate existing Skyrim mods, we've been able to implement replacements that we think fit Skyblivion's needs, in some cases even better than what we had before."

However, Rebel and co claim that despite them making it "clear multiple times to this former volunteer that we have removed their contributions", the ex-Skyblivion dev is "threatening to sue for damages upwards of €30,000". They claim that the ex-volunteer's legal threats "demand personal information of multiple volunteers [on Skyblivion] including full names and addresses". Rebel noted that the team see these demands as "something that we are simply not willing to share with someone that we don't even know" and feel are "just completely disproportionate for what's really going on".

The modders say they've consulted with legal counsel already and have a lawyer on standby if necessary. Though, since said lawyer's services will - the Skyblivion team claim - cost €2,500, they've put out a call for anyone with "a background in IP law or GDPR law" willing to offer them pro bono legal aid to get in touch via the mod's website.

"Please don't turn this into any kind of witch hunt, despite this very unfortunate situation," Rebel said in closing. "We don't wish ill on a former volunteer over all this and I just hope that we can get this resolved as soon as possible and get on with the planned release, which is really what we're working towards. You will hear more from us soon on the actual release."

This situation makes it two years running that Skyblivion's found itself engulfed in drama during the final months of what's supposed to be its release year. In 2025, former volunteer Dee Keyes had a public disagreement with the project's leads over whether releasing the mod that year was a reasonable or achievable goal. Skyblivion was subsequently delayed into 2026.

This past weekend, Keyes tweeted a response to the Skyblivion team's statement on the alleged legal threats. "I've had my issues with the project and left because of it, but I left knowing that my work would remain with [Skyblivion] (happily so) and didn't want to hurt the project's progress," he wrote. "I understand [the former volunteer] being upset, but I really don't see why they'd go so far as to demand their work ripped out."

Here's hoping the Skyblivion team and the ex-volunteer can resolve things without all the expense and effort that'd inevitably be necessary if the dispute ends up in court. Given there are now less than two months left of 2026, and Skyblivion's modders have this on their plates on top of any remaining work needed to finish their creation, I'd personally be very surprised if its release doesn't end up being pushed into next year.

#4077. Guide: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

Probably the most anticipated game of all time, GTA 6 is now less than one week away!

As the launch draws even closer, we're covering absolutely everything you need to know about its PS5 launch, including preload options and release times. In this GTA 6 guide, we cover the GTA 6 release times.

On this page: GTA 6 Release Times: When Can You Start Playing?

Rockstar has confirmed GTA 6 will officially be playable from midnight on 19th November in your local time zone. If you have preloaded the game, it'll unlock at midnight, and then you can begin playing immediately.

As such, the game will unlock and be available first in New Zealand. Availability will then roll out worldwide as each time zone reaches midnight on 19th November.

GTA 6 preload is available now! If you've pre-ordered from the PS Store, your download of the game should have started and will then be ready for you to start playing at release.

Rockstar has now officially confirmed the GTA 6 file size on PS5, and what you'll need to download, is 212GB. This is one of the biggest downloads and installs on console in history, and will probably only get bigger through patches and the addition of GTA Online.

GTA 6 will unlock and be playable in New Zealand first, as it's located in one of the furthest along timezones. The chances are New Zealand is further along in the day compared to wherever you live in the world, so yes, New Zealand will be the first to gain access to GTA 6.

Because of this, there's been a rising trend in people creating New Zealand PSN account to play games as soon as possible. This can be done with GTA 6 too, but you'll need to set up a fresh New Zealand PSN account and buy the game through its PS Store.

When you have done, you'll be able to play GTA 6 a few hours ahead of other countries like the USA. Keep in mind, though, that you can't transfer your save data from the New Zealand account you set up to your normal profile.

GTA 6 is available digitally on the PS Store, or in a basic physical version that ships without a disc. The latter provides a code in the box that you redeem on the PS Store to get the digital version.

The two PS5 digital versions on offer are: Standard Edition and Ultimate Edition.

Ultimate Edition / Ultimate Edition Upgrade Contents:

Rockstar is only selling GTA 6 in a digital format; you can't buy the game on a physical disc in any way. Even the version you buy in retail shops or from online retailers won't contain a disc. Instead, the actual GTA 6 box will have a code inside you can use to download the game. There's no version with a physical disc of any kind.

Rockstar has now confirmed a GTA 6 map will be made available, but it won't be included in the physical versions like for previous games. Instead, a physical GTA 6 map will be put on the official Rockstar store for $0.99. Or, it'll be included for free in all other purchases from the storefront.

Have you pre-ordered GTA 6, and will you be staying up to play at midnight? Let us know in the comments below.

#4076. Asha Sharma Issues Statement On Xbox's 25th Anniversary And The Future Of Gaming

"Our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games"

We've been waiting all week for Xbox to acknowledge its 25th anniversary in a formal fashion, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has now issued a statement discussing the past, present and future of the brand to celebrate its birthday.

It's a pretty lengthy statement, and a lot of it is just about recapping the history of Xbox and Microsoft Gaming as a whole. Sharma talks about how things have come a long way since "Microsoft Adventure" in 1979, and then how Xbox was "impossible to miss" in 2001 while also revolutionising online play and being there for the launch of Halo.

There's also a cool high-definition ad for the original Xbox console that you can see down below.

"When the original XBOX launched in 2001, it was impossible to miss. It was 2-3x larger than rival consoles, with a giant X molded into a black enclosure and a bright alien green jewel at the center..."

"A year later, Xbox Live revolutionized online play with persistent friend lists and matchmaking, as well as a common service for developers to build connected experiences. And bringing all of this together was Halo: Combat Evolved, a launch title that not only defined XBOX but proved its first advertising campaign: “Games Will Never Be The Same.”

After going through the history, Sharma mentions that each of the 111 people who have worked at Xbox since the beginning will be getting "a special engraved console to commemorate what you’ve helped build".

She then references the fans, Xbox FanFest and how today's FanFest event in Seattle will "bring the celebration home".

"The story of XBOX has never been ours alone. Our fans have challenged us, cheered us on, held us accountable, and stuck with us. We’ve been celebrating this anniversary with fans around the world and special launches. Today, we are bringing the celebration home to Seattle."

And finally, the most notable bit in this statement is probably what she says about the "next 25" years of Xbox, highlighting that the "cost, resources, and risk required" to create modern games has grown dramatically, and that it's had an impact on the ability to turn ideas into games, or at least allow those ideas to reach their potential.

As a result, she says it's something that "must" be changed, and that people and small teams will "soon" be able to achieve things that currently require much larger teams and financial resources in today's world.

"While modern games demonstrate the heights of human craft in ways unimaginable just decades ago, the cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown just as dramatically. As a result, too many ideas never become games, and too many games fall short of what their creators imagined. For decades, this has been the unavoidable tradeoff of ambition. We must change this."

"Throughout human history, the scale of what we could create was determined by the people, capital, and resources we could command. That relationship is beginning to break. A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations. A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers and hundreds of millions of dollars. And our largest studios will be able to pursue ambitions as far beyond today’s games as Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 is from its first entry in 1982."

"I believe the future of gaming will look more like its beginning, when a small team with a big idea could change how the world plays. Our responsibility is to deliver great games, unmistakable hardware, and give more people the chance to make something the world has never seen."

There's some interesting stuff in here for sure, and we reckon it might be worth keeping an eye on tonight's Seattle Xbox FanFest event for any potential announcements - after all, it's the final stop and "home" destination for the FanFest tour.

For now though, let us know what you think about Asha Sharma's statement down below!

Yes. The passage is strongly AI-related, although it never explicitly mentions artificial intelligence.

It appears to be alluding to the transformative potential of AI, particularly generative AI, in video game development.

1. "A single person will soon be able to wield capabilities that once required entire nations."

2. "A small team will be able to build worlds that today demand hundreds of developers."

3. "The cost, resources, and risk required to create them have grown dramatically."

No. The passage deliberately avoids mentioning AI, machine learning, or generative AI.

The underlying message is that AI and emerging technology will fundamentally change the economics and scale of video game development.

The author is suggesting that the next generation of games will be created with fewer people, fewer resources, and significantly greater creative ambition.

The wording is particularly interesting because it frames AI not simply as a way to cut jobs or costs, but as a way to enable creative possibilities that were previously impossible.

My verdict: I would interpret this as an indirect statement about the future of AI in gaming, with AI likely being a major part of the vision, even though the passage carefully avoids naming it directly.

I'm probably in the minority here, @HonestHick, but I really do not care if a game is made entirely by AI (which it surely will at some point!).

The way I look at it is that AI is just a natural progression of the technological revolution. Just as with the Industrial Revolution, humans will adapt to it happening, and will find other means of employment, and just as with the Industrial Revolution it won't happen all at once, it will be a gradual process of replacing certain tasks within game development, with the dynamic of who does what changing over many years rather than all of a sudden. In a decade, when AI involvement will be much greater, it will be largely accepted that this is the way games get made. Right now, there is resistance within the gaming community, but as time goes on, and AI usage becomes more prevalent, so too will the acceptance of the gaming community that this is the way of things.

I think what will sway things is that games will be made faster; potentially a lot faster. AAA games that take 5 to 7 years to make now, will be made in 2 to 3 years, and then possibly fewer than that as AI improves and is more deeply implemented.

What should also happen, is that games will cost a lot less to be made, and hopefully that will be passed on to the consumer. If a game costs £200 million to be made now, it needs to be sold at £70 in the hope of recouping that money. With AI heavily involved, that development costs far, far less, and I think those companies that pass on those savings to the gaming community may find that it is very much appreciated.

So, if games can be made more quickly, and cost less, then I personally do not see the downsides of that because regardless of AI humans will always be involved somewhere along the process...

First of all, nobody was talking specifically about AI. AI is only one part of the tools that are available today to make game development easier. For years now, development tools and resources have become increasingly accessible to small teams and even to solo developers. Just remember Bright Memory, released in 2019 and developed by a single person using Unreal Engine. Back then, AI wasn't even being discussed the way it is today. Several of these tools are free, including Unreal Engine, and if you're passionate enough, you can develop a game on your own or with a small team without needing a massive budget.

As for AI, yes, of course it speeds up production processes. But that's not a bad thing. In fact, it's mostly a positive when you actually understand the topic. It can also significantly reduce production costs without sacrificing quality when used properly. I use AI every day, and it really depends on how you use it. It all comes down to what tasks you delegate to AI, how you use it, and what you keep as a human-driven creative process, especially when it comes to artistic decisions.

#4075. Delve into "a deep underground facility full of secrets and horrors" in the latest Fallout 4 quest mod from the Commonwealth Story Expansion Project

A mysterious bunker with out of this world contents

After adding a whole new town to Fallout 4 last month, a group of modders have released another in their long string of extra quests for the RPG. This latest mission revolves around a dungeon delve in the Glowing Sea, where a mysterious bunker's just been unearthed.

"The harsh radioactive winds of the Glowing Sea have uncovered a deep underground facility full of secrets and horrors," the group behind the Commonwealth Story Expansion Project (CSEP) declared the description of this latest work, Under The Stars.

A fresh dungeon with a quest attached, the mod tasks you with donning your hazmat suit for a trip to a sunken bunker in the region of post-apocalyptic Boston with the least chill weather. Inside await voiced holotapes and puzzles offering clues as to what went down in this cosy corner of the Commonwealth, plus some new gear to make braving whatever lurks within worth it.

Spoilers: Judging by the screenshots, it looks like the place is an Area 51-esque hidey-hole for evidence of aliens and other cryptic oddities.

If you're unfamiliar, the CSEP lot are responsible for a bunch of popular Fallout 4 quest mods based around the likes of deadly cults, underground wars, post-apocalyptic detective work, and Brotherhood of Steel drama. While Under The Stars doesn't look have been as big an undertaking as those, that previous form points to it being an expertly-crafted addition that'll slot seamlessly into the game.

The modders have put Under The Stars together as part of a community-hosted modding jam called Fallout Flood, with this latest one based around the theme of being underground. Among the other works to have come out of it thus far are another Fallout 4 quest mod dubbed Stranded - The Oasis, a dungeon full of funky rats called the S'Laven, and a new robot enemy you can wear as a hat. It's also produced a New Vegas quest mod about exploring an abandoned NCR railway, so seems to have been very productive gathering of modding minds.

To give Under The Stars a go, your copy of Fallout 4 will need to have the Automatron and Vault-Tec Workshop DLCs.

#4074. Christopher Nolan confirms what we all suspected: there's a bit of Oppenheimer in The Odyssey ending

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Keep exploring and earning more as a member.

Get the biggest gaming news, reviews, and releases straight to your inbox.

Bringing all the latest movie news, features, and reviews to your inbox

Get full access to premium articles, exclusive features and a growing list of member rewards.

Christopher Nolan changes the way you watch The Odyssey’s ending with this one observation about his career

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Christopher Nolan is, famously, never one to discuss his movie's endings at length. So when he does talk, we invariably listen.

Speaking at a Q&A moderated by Robert Downey Jr. (and documented for posterity by The Nerd Wire), Nolan confirmed what many had suspected – The Odyssey's ending deliberately echoes his previous film Oppenheimer.

"I was finding Oppenheimer [and] I was finding a little bit of [my other films] in there," Nolan said.

"As I wrote the end, I suddenly found a bit of Oppenheimer in there – that sort of connection. I was looking at my notebooks the other day, somewhere I scribbled as I wrote the ending: this is the ending of all my films rolled into one."

The Odyssey's ending, lest we forget, features Odysseus sailing from Ithaca but left with the memory of his and his men's actions in Troy – at a tipping point in civilization where it appears the boundaries of society are beginning to collapse. By comparison, Oppenheimer also saw its lead wrestling with profound guilt and an immense change in the world we live in.

Downey Jr., who won Best Supporting Actor under Nolan's direction as Lewis Strauss in Oppenheimer, also pointed out parallels between Oppenheimer's ending and that of Dunkirk, which features a burning plane in much the same way Nolan focuses on the Trojan Horse in flames in the Troy-set flashbacks.

"It's crazy, because it never feels like you're repeating anything but there's concentric circles of plumbing new depths along these themes," Downey Jr., commented.

The Odyssey, set for home release on November 17, because Nolan's most successful film at the box office – grossing over $1.8 billion. It stars Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Zendaya, and Tom Holland, with plenty of early whispers that it will be among the Best Picture frontrunners at next year's Academy Awards.

For more, we have a complete breakdown of The Odyssey ending, plus a ranking of the best Christopher Nolan movies.

OwlCat Games has unveiled fresh gameplay from The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, and the sci-fi RPG continues to look really promising.

Now that we're past all of the drama with the game's male protagonist — his default appearance was recently changed along with his voice after a lot of critical feedback — it's time to take a look the female lead.

She's all over this new gameplay montage, which showcases characters, dialogue, a little bit of exploration, and a bunch of zero-g combat. It's probably one of the title's best trailers to date.

However, we still don't have a release date for this one. All we know for sure is that it's launching next year, and that it's got a spring 2027 target — but if that's going to stick, then we'll be needing a concrete date sooner rather than later.

I suppose it's also worth noting that a direct competitor to Osiris Reborn — fellow Mass Effect-style RPG Exodus — is locked in for the 7th April. Ideally, these two don't want to go head-to-head and potentially cannibalise each other's initial sales.

#4071. DOOM Developer id Software Confirms It's Working On A New Game

id Software, the developer known for FPS hits such as DOOM and Quake, has confirmed it's got a new game in the pipeline.

Alongside the news about Wolfenstein 3, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma revealed how id is also "working on its next game". id Software elaborated on this, mentioning how its next project, led by Hugo Martin, comes from its teams located in Texas and Frankfurt.

Just don't expect to hear about it too soon. Here's the full message:

id Software: "We're incredibly excited about our next project, a new game from our teams in Texas and Frankfurt, with game direction once again by Hugo Martin. It'll be some time before we're ready to share more but we can't wait for you to see what we're working on."

According to The Verge's senior correspondent Tom Warren, this project is a "new Doom game". Here's what he had to say in response to id Software news on social media:

"I reported in July that id were in the “early stages of a new Doom game” and now it’s confirmed."

This follows the news earlier this year of layoffs at id Software, which led to a statement from the studio, noting how the team was now "about the same size" as it was when making DOOM (2016).

id Software has previously released DOOM and DOOM Eternal on the Switch with the help of Panic Button. As for now, there's been no mention about it bringing across its latest title, DOOM: The Dark Ages, to Nintendo's new hybrid platform.

#4070. Xbox Playback Is Now Available, Take A Look Back At Your Xbox History

"Your games. Your milestones. Your story."

One of my favourite things to do is look back at the Xbox games I've been playing, the achievements I've unlocked, and all of my cool unique stats that make me the Xbox gamer I am.

This year, Xbox is doing something a bit different. Unlike previous Xbox 'Year in Review' roundups, which cover the past 11 or 12 months, Xbox Playback takes things all the way back to the beginning, celebrating your story through Xbox's 25 years.

You can access your own Xbox Playback from the official Xbox site, where you'll need to sign in with your Microsoft account. There's this whole song-and-dance animation, sorta like Spotify's Wrapped, which takes you through stuff like the first game you played, what year you played the most, what % of most played time across all of Xbox, achievements, and loads of other really cool stuff. Then, you can share it to social media if you fancy.

As you can see above, Xbox CTO Scott Van Vliet created his account in 2006, has earned 28,528 gamerscore, and has 4,375 hours played: which is only in the top 4.8% of hours played, whereas yours truly is in the 0.2%. What can I say? I guess I'm an Xbox gamer after all.

Another thing that's really cool about Xbox Playback is that, for the first time ever, players will be able to access and view it directly from their console. No browser required. According to Xbox, it should appear soon, so keep an eye out!

We're keen to find out what your Xbox Playback says about your journey with Xbox through the years, so please do let us know what that looks like down in the comments. What percentage of hours played are you? What was your first game? When did you join? Let us hear it!

#4069. Fewer genAI clones of "someone else's specific game" should flood the net going forwards, as Anthropic tell Claude to stop messing with some stuff other people own

It will still let people generate "original" games using the tech

Anthropic have told their genAI tool Claude to start ducking requests from users to recreate or clone existing games, following a flood of folks using the tech to generate six-fingered remakes. Instead of risking infringing on the intellectual property of series or titles that companies which aren't Anthropic own, Claude will instead restrict itself to only generating "original" games slopped together based on whatever data it's drawing on.

"We added two sentences to Claude Code's prompt on Opus 5.5 to steer it away from recreating someone else's specific game because using Claude to infringe IP is against our usage policy," Anthropic staffer Addy Osmani wrote on not Twitter in response to a rando with a cat profile picture having spotted the change.

"Original games, genre games, and games built from your own designs and assets are meant to keep working," Osmani continued. "We'll continue to iterate to ensure we're striking the right balance. In the meantime, if Claude turns down something that's yours, send it my way." Game Developer reached out to Anthropic for confirmation and were pointed to Osmani's post.

The change should make it harder to add to the horde of genAI-powered decomps, recomps, and ports which have hit the net recently. It's hardly a surprising one, given studios like Bethesda have seemingly had to take matters into their own lawyers' hands to get the likes of an AI-generated Fallout game taken offline, with games that've just been ripped wholesale or barely tweaked likely on even more perilous ground. That said, not every corp's responded to the DIY decompilation craze by immediately taking legal action.

There's a serious degree of irony to Anthropic slapping Claude and telling it stealing is bad. One of the ways the company develop and train their genAI models is by scraping publicly available data from the internet via a web crawler.

So, some nicking of stuff is bad, little bot people keep asking to regurgitate stuff into slop they can then try to pass off as something they've created. But not all nicking of stuff, lest our whole business be on rather shaky ground.

It's unlikely this move from Anthropic does much to convince actual developers of original games they're safe to put demos of their games out prior to release, without risking dickheads using genAI to clone said demo and potentially release a slop version in rapid fashion, but one can dream of that genie being put back in the bottle someday.

#4068. Tom Holland says working on The Odyssey gave him a "level of confidence as an actor" he's never had before

Join the GamesRadar community for quick access. Enter your email below and we'll send confirmation, and sign you up to our newsletter.

Tom Holland says he is "very grateful" to Christopher Nolan for giving him "a level of confidence as an actor that I don't think I had before"

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Not only is Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey one of the most successful movies of the year, but it has marked a pivotal point in star Tom Holland's career, who says he now has a new level of confidence and ambition to take on even bigger projects.

"I've been an admirer of Chris since I can remember, so having the opportunity to work with him and have his approval and sit in his house and watch his movie and to get a pat on the back was just the perfect way for me to start whatever it is I'm doing next," said Holland at a recent The Odyssey Q&A in London, shared online by Twitter user @Woow_Lucas. "It's confidence and ambition to see what else is out there for me."

The actor, who plays Odysseus' son Telemachus in the epic, added, "He's given me a level of confidence as an actor that I don't think I had before, and I'm very grateful that that is something I can take away from this. I think going into my next project with this sense of achievement is newfound confidence in what I think I can do."

The movie adapts Homer's ancient Greek poem of the same name, following Matt Damon as King of Ithaca Odysseus on his perilous decade-long journey home after the Trojan War. Back in Ithaca, Holland's Telemachus fights off his mother's suitors who are eyeing up his father's throne. But when he is visited by a strange traveller who tells him that his father is alive, Telemachus sets in motion a plan for a safe reinstatement.

This was certainly a different role for Holland, who we are used to seeing suited up as the MCU's Spider-Man. The Odyssey opened to rave reviews, earning a whopping $1.8 billion worldwide in total. The movie was so in demand that it sold out IMAX screens for months. But it's not just the success of the movie that has had an effect on its cast.

The project was shot on location around the world, from remote caves in Greece to the open sea, where Nolan got through 400 miles of film. Damon has opened up about how difficult yet joyous the whole experience was, saying he didn't sleep for days but just rolled with the punches, as he felt that he would never make a movie like it again.

#4067. For Its Home Console Debut, New PS5 Professor Layton Game Ups the Price to $65

Professor Layton and apprentice Luke aren't playing about with small handheld Nintendo DS and 3DS releases anymore; they're in the big leagues now with a proper PS5 and Switch 2 release. Professor Layton and the New World of Steam is the first time the series has appeared on a home console, and the price of the new entry matches that: £53.99 / $64.99.

Compared to previous titles in the franchise, this is a significant price increase — the DS and 3DS games were generally around $30 to $40 at launch, increasing as the series went on. Now, as the New World of Steam plans for a December 2026 release, it'll cost roughly double the price of Professor Layton and the Curious Village, which was the first game in the series.

It'll be interesting to see how much the PS5 remake of that costs when it comes out next year.

Nevertheless, this is no longer a PS5 game in impulse-purchase territory; Professor Layton and the New World of Steam is only $5 cheaper than Marvel's Wolverine!

As it makes the jump onto home consoles, Level-5 is promising the most puzzles in the series, a brand new exploration system, and a new puzzle added to the game every day for over a year after its launch in December.

Pre-orders are live now on the PS Store ahead of the 12th December 2026 release. Do you think this is a fair price for a Professor Layton game or not? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

#4066. Round Up: The Reviews Are In For Metaphor: ReFantazio's Switch 2 Port

Metaphor: ReFantazio brings more JRPG action to the Switch 2 this week, and the reviews are now rolling in.

Starting with our own here on Nintendo Life, we thought it was an extradinary experience, but couldn't look past the poor optimisation in the Switch 2 version.

"Anyone looking for a huge, sprawling adventure with lovable characters, compelling parallels to the real world, and progression systems that will keep you coming back for more will be far from disappointed with this game, but there's no metaphor for a dodgy frame rate and visuals that can occasionally take you out of the fantasy."

Review Metaphor: ReFantazio (Switch 2) - An Extraordinary JRPG That Could Use Another Optimisation Pass

"Metaphor: ReFantazio is a fantastic, fresh new take on the Persona formula, and the Switch 2 is one of the best ways to play it. With very little in the way of compromises, Atlus has delivered a solid port that makes one of its best games in years available to players of the best handheld console on the market."

"As a video game, though, I can’t recommend Metaphor: ReFantazio enough. It set a really high standard for job systems, time management, and dungeon crawling in an RPG. There’s just so much tight, considered design all over the experience, and the story still feels relevant today...While I wish the port was better, it’s been nice to revisit my favorite ATLUS game on my favorite system."

"This is a full-scope JRPG that comes dangerously close to being 100 hours without feeling like it could be consolidated down in any way, and it’s playable on the go. I do think that we sometimes forget to consider that it wasn’t that long ago that the compromises that it took to get games onto handheld consoles meant that such devices didn’t really work as the primary gaming device for most people. Yeah, the Switch 2 might not have the power of the PlayStation 5, but it’s to look at something like this running on it and think to yourself, “you know what? Close enough.”

This is a fantastic, imaginative tale that’s worth retelling. It speaks to the power of dreaming for a greater life and standing united against charismatic tyranny on a grand stage. It manages that while still giving its cast their own smaller moments to shine and without losing sight of being an excellent video game...it’s an ode to what’s possible when creatives set aside the safer path and strive for originality — something this industry could use more of while celebrating and holding fast to the talent that brings art to life.

"If you’re an RPG fan who’s especially fond of the offerings that come from Atlus, Metaphor: ReFantazio is a dead simple recommendation. While the story might not be for everyone, the excellent combat and novel Archetype progression system are worth the price of admission for folks whose love of all things turn-based burns bright. Applying a fantasy coat of paint to the demon realms of SMT and the real world settings of Persona works wonders, and it’s a welcome sight to see Atlus step outside of their sequel tradition and try something new. The Switch 2 version makes for a worthy ship on which to take this voyage, with options to adjust the experience based on your preference for performance or graphical fidelity. You might be here for a long time, but Metaphor is like a familiar friend LARP-ing in a high fantasy world."

"Between its combat, characters, politics, music, and striking fantasy world, Metaphor: ReFantazio is still one of Atlus’ best games of all time. Whether played docked or taken on the go, the Switch 2 version gives another audience a good excuse to finally experience it."

If you want to try before you buy, there's also a demo you can check out and save data will carry over to the full game.

#4065. Fix up towering robots while battle rages outside in Bay 12: Mech Repair, a first-person job sim with some handsome heavy duty analog tech

The most important thing to know about Bay 12: Mech Repair is that these are mechs of the MechWarrior or possibly Patlabor school – that is, basically WW2 tanks on hydraulic legs, with cockpits full of switches and wireframe displays. Their bodies are assemblages of pistons and reactors. They are not biomechs like the ones in Evangelion. An Evangelion Repair game would be… different. Less industrial, more Oedipal. You would dread removing the smallest piece of housing.

Which isn't to say that Bay 12: Mech Repair represents life on Easy Street, exactly. There's a big war happening outside, its fortunes palpable in the minced leg joints and pocked torsos of the war-bots lowered into your hangar. You're also fed details about the lives of pilots when you accept a work order. Lieutenant Iona Vale of the 3rd Recon Company says there's "left leg hesitation after extended operation", especially at higher temperatures. That sure sounds like a thing that could get Lieutenant Iona Vale killed.

It's not clear whether you can diagnose faults incorrectly, and shape the progress of the conflict, but the context brings extra emotional charge to what might otherwise be a cosy process of glueing together very expensive Air-Fix models, for all the sense of scale.

Bay 12: Mech Repair follows a familiar flow, as job sims go. Banged-up Iron Giants arrive in a steady procession. You figure out what's wrong with them based on scans, pilot reports, and so forth. Then you get out there with a welder, drill and spanner to make it right. Busted parts can be salvaged for scrap for custom components. Completed work orders net you credits that must be divided between restocking your inventory and buying new tools.

You also have the option of clearing away rust and applying a new paintjob. I'm fascinated to know if this has any real impact on either the story or your fortunes, because I guarantee that I am going to spend far more time obsessing over dazzle camouflage than giving the ol' actuators a haircut.

Read more on Steam. The devs, Crimson Herring Studios, are them wot did Sovereign Syndicate, an apparently decent Victorian fantasy RPG that we never found time to review. Look, I am not made of thumbs and eyeballs. As for the daunting possibility of an Evangelion Fixing Sim, the recently announced Valkyrie Iteration gets into some of the squirming detail, there.

#4064. Hang On, Firefight Is Coming To Halo: Campaign Evolved

Halo: Campaign Evolved isn't dead, people!

Firefight has just been announced as a free update for Halo: Campaign Evolved, arriving sometime this winter. The series' staple co-op PvE mode is locked in, with more details set to be shared at Halo Fest on December 12-13.

Halo: Campaign Evolved received some backlash for its lack of multiplayer options, particularly PvP and Firefight. I thought the criticism was understandable, but perhaps a little unfair given the game was always marketed as a campaign remake.

"For nearly two decades, Firefight has been a Halo favorite, challenging Spartans to team up, hold the line, and survive wave after wave of enemies. The tradition continues this winter as we add the four-player cooperative PvE mode to Halo: Campaign Evolved in a free update.

We’re kicking things off tonight at XBOX FanFest, where attendees will be the first to jump in and experience Firefight across new maps and armed with plenty of weapons to help even the odds."

Forgive my opening sentiment, but I honestly wasn't expecting anything new to come from Halo Studios. Especially after the developer was essentially reduced to a skeleton team, with future Halo production being handed over to Activision.

I'm a huge fan of Halo: Campaign Evolved, and whilst I'm still sad the teased Halo 2 remake seems unlikely, you should have seen me leap out of my seat when I spotted the announcement that Firefight was on its way. Hoorah!

#4063. You can make a vampire hunter who's afraid of the dark, disease and small spaces in Hunter: The Reckoning - Deathwish, and that's surely the best way to play

A month or two back I penned a 1500 word whine about feeling too powerful in Blood of Dawnwalker. "Gimme a vampire sim in which I'm a pathetic vein-nibbling goblin," I wrote, using many more adjectives than that. Well, never let it be said that I'm biased against vampires, for I am equally keen to play an RPG in which I am the least capable vampire hunter in the universe. A vampire hunter who screams when he wakes up with his hair over his face. A vampire hunter who has to spray the vampires with antibac before staking them.

An RPG like Hunter: The Reckoning – Deathwish, perhaps, which presents you with a choice of Advantages and Flaws when creating a character. You have to balance these out on a gnarly weighing scale, before they'll let you through the game's front door. Here is a video showing all that off, together with a lot of sixpacks.

The Advantage/Flaw system looks familiar on the surface. Advantages include Warrior, which gives you +15% chance of a critical hit, or Charmer, which gives you a +1 to Persuasion skill checks. Flaws include clumsy, bad reputation, fear of darkness, hypochondriac, and claustrophobia.

I don't know much about the tabletop game on which Deathwish is based, and the video skims the detail here, but I suspect the last three Flaws will boil down to something like "-1 Constitution in Unlit Closets". Still, I really enjoy the idiocy of going up against crypt-dwelling undead while being unable to tolerate shadows, small spaces, and disease. In general, I'd love it if Hunter: The Reckoning – Deathwish steered well away from any possibility of simply overpowering the vamps, to say nothing of the werewolves and other creatures of the night.

This appears to be the idea: devs Teyon have stressed their desire to make something more story and investigation-driven, after the stomping gibfest that was RoboCop: Rogue City. As narrative designer Mateusz Działowski put it in a previous dev diary, they've "switched from action with RPG elements into RPG with action elements". Amongst other things, you'll need to put together a team of fellow would-be slayers, each with secrets and traumas, and gather clues about best tactics while roaming the game's condensed and shiny New York City. You can read more about it all on Steam.

Following the news of Elizabeth Olsen's return as a Wanda Maximoff and a tease that Paul Bettany will be back as Vision in Avengers: Doomsday, another star has hinted at their return.

In her new podcast, Gwyneth Paltrow interviewed Zoe Saldaña as the pair bonded over not having any idea what they were doing on the set of Avengers: Endgame. "Well, first of all, I hadn't seen any of the movies," Paltrow jokes on The Goop Guide. "You can't read the script because they think they're literally the CIA and there's password protection."

However, what's most intriguing about their chat is that Paltrow goes on to say that she's had a similar experience recently too.

"I used to make a lot of movies; those are very specific in terms of the changing and the secrecy, and I was going to say something but I'm not allowed to say, so I'll tell you later," she says, before adding: "I mean it's not a big deal, believe me, but it was just I had an experience relatively recently where I was like, again, 'What am I doing? While she doesn't actually name the movie, Marvel fans are pretty convinced that she's talking about Avengers: Doomsday. Reacting to the moment on social media, one tweeted: "Gwyneth Paltrow, look me in the eyes and tell me Pepper Potts will be back in Doomsday, I'm going insane." #4061. Zelda Ocarina's ReDead Were Set To Be "Very, Very Scary" In The Remake, But Nintendo Decided To "Dial It Back"

The team maybe went "a step too far", according to the producer

Ocarina of Time Remake isn't really a scary game, but there are still some enemies throughout this adventure that may give players a fright.

Perhaps the most notable are ReDead, the zombie-like creatures that are difficult to escape when they set their sights on Link. These return in the remake and apparently were even scarier at one point during development, until Nintendo decided to "dial it back".

Here's what producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi had to say about this during a recent interview with GameSpot:

"With this remake, the graphics are a lot improved, and so the ReDead–the sound, the graphics, and the movement–ended up being very, very scary. And the staff wanted to make this in service of making a good gameplay experience. But from our perspective, taking a step back, we felt like, let’s remember the experience that we don’t want to change, and taking that into consideration, maybe we’ve gone a step too far, so let’s dial it back."

So, the decision was made to ensure the experience was more in line with the original game. The final result is the ReDead are still somewhat scary, but not "very, very scary" to the point it changes the experience.

Soapbox Losing Control - Why Zelda’s ReDead Strike Fear Into Our Souls

Do you think Nintendo got the ReDead right in this remake? Would you have been up for an even scarier version of these enemies in the Switch 2 release? Let us know your thoughts in the comments.

#4060. itch.io will soon let you filter games with genAI disclosures out of your search results on the site, after admitting it was previously "critically lacking"

itch.io has unfortunately, much like Steam, long had an issue with genAI content being uploaded in droves, drowning out perfectly good games made by human hands. The apparent standard method against this, voluntary genAI disclosure, has been itch's primary tool to combat this wave of low-quality slop, but hasn't worked out too well; itch revealed a few days ago that 'the number of game pages being created per-day has doubled in the past two months'. Now, in attempts to further combat this, beyond just game assets requiring a genAI disclosure to upload as they have for two years, itch will be expanding the mandatory disclosure to tabletop games, books, comics, and soundtracks, as well as adding a 'no AI' filter directly into the search function.

itch noted in this announcement that its previous moderation of genAI use in projects had been "critically lacking", presumably referring to the unfathomable exponential increase in games being uploaded in the past few months by people who don't give a fuck about creating anything themselves and happily contribute to the death of the planet. itch went on to post "Just deleted a couple terabytes of ai slop" which, I mean, sure, cool! And, look, as many, many people in itch's replies have pointed out, this is not the same as outright banning AI.

Unfortunately, my question at that point becomes: how? itch is not Steam, not a storefront backed by a gigantic corporation with support staff and quality assurance (which, you know, hasn't helped Steam much either). itch is one full-time employee with several contractors and volunteers. If there is a site-wide ban on genAI, people who use genAI will just start lying and sneaking it into their projects anyway. So, then, users just report the offenders, surely? This then requires a manual verification system, which, as is suggested by the sheer amount of games being uploaded every day, is just not feasible, let alone for a team as small as itch. And, frankly, I don't have a better solution here! This is fucked! What itch is doing is, currently, kinda the best it can right now?

itch is a beautiful thing that allows for people who just want to start making games, making art, making music, making books, to have a free space to share it with the world, and gain eyes on their work as well as necessary feedback to improve. It's less of a store and more of a forum for creators and self-published games to interact, guide one another to new, niche, cool shit. Hell, I made a visual novel and posted it on there, becoming another one of those millions of people for whom itch is a valuable platform for first creations. To have this vital space on a path to ruin as a result of the same vile tech that is also on the verge of pushing the global economy over a cliff due to its creators being caught in their multi-year lies is not a future I hope for itch. This is a step in the right direction, and one I genuinely hope pans out well for it in the long run.

#4059. MMO Horizon Steel Frontiers 'Nearing Completion', NC Discussing Release Timing with Sony

While the future may look bleak for series creator Guerrilla’s own Horizon multiplayer game, Korean partner NC has confirmed to investors that its MMO spin-off Horizon Steel Frontiers is “nearing completion”.

Korean outlet News1 quotes co-CEO Park Byung-moo as saying: “The new Horizon IP game is nearing completion. We are continuously discussing the release timing with the IP holder, Sony, and plan to make an announcement soon.”

For those who don’t know, Horizon Steel Frontiers is a spin-off mobile MMO being developed under license from Sony.

So far, it’s only been officially announced for release in Asian countries, although NC has noted demand from PS5 players who’d like to play this on console.

Currently the game is scheduled to release in 2027 on mobile platforms and PC via the company’s Purple emulator.

Sony’s approach to mobile has been confusing for decades now; it recently announced plans to pull the plug on a Ratchet & Clank spin-off, which was in beta on smartphones.

Rather than actively promote Horizon Steel Frontiers, the platform holder has put its weight behind Guerrilla’s abovementioned co-op game Horizon Hunters Gathering, which is being retooled after receiving a negative response earlier in the year and has until December to find a fresh path forward.

It’s going to be beyond embarrassing for the manufacturer if NC’s MMO makes it to market and is proven to be a success, while series creator Guerrilla’s version is cancelled, as is looking like a possibility right now.

#4058. Three Special Football Jerseys Go On Sale To Celebrate Halo's 25th Anniversary

I've always had a thing for video game edition sports tees. They're breathable, durable, a bit weighted, and usually feature something subtle from a game I like on the front.

Xbox and sportswear company Dyenamik have already teamed up in recent weeks with to ship a range of gorgeous Xbox 25th Anniversary shirts. Now they're back with a new collection of Halo Anniversary tees, and they're looking very tempting.

The Halo shirts seem to be on available now if you fancy popping one in your sports bag. Individually, they'll set you back £70, with worldwide shipping available. Alternatively, you can grab all three in a Limited Edition Anniversary collection box for £175. Just be mindful that only 200 boxes were made, so you'll want to be quick!

So, let's go through them - here's a look at all three:

The legend himself. A black jersey carrying a grey halftone print of the Master Chief's helmet, scaled up across the back and wrapping around the front, with crisp white piping, a white HALO wordmark and the Master Chief's helmet just below the collar on the back.

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

A tribute to the olive green MJOLNIR armour that made Spartan-117 the face of Halo. Black side panels, a black hexagonal pattern cascading across the shoulders and fading down the back, and chevron-striped cuffs, with 117 running down the left sleeve and the Master Chief's helmet and the UNSC eagle on the chest.

The AI who guided the Chief across the first Halo ring. The jersey fades from bright cyan to deep navy like her holographic form, with fine horizontal lines running through it like streams of data. White piping, Cortana's data chip and the UNSC eagle finish the front, with the Halo ring emblem just below the collar on the back.

A premium branded box finished in silver foil, with space to store and display all three jerseys together, kept the way a Spartan keeps their kit. Only 200 boxes are available, made for the fans who have been finishing the fight since 2001, and this collection is the only way to get one.

What do you think? Initially, I thought the black one was my favourite, but the blue Cortana jersey is growing on me. It is ultra vibrant and a perfect tone of blue.

£70 is no joke for a shirt, but it seems to be par for the course when it comes to sportswear these days. The Xbox 25th Anniversary collection is bleddy lush too, so worth checking those out whilst you're at it!

A well-timed audio upgrade could make all the difference

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

What many are calling the biggest game of the decade is nearly upon us, but there's still time to fill out your setup ahead of Rockstar's release. Finding the best headset for GTA 6 means working out what you want from your experience, and which audio features the game itself will actually be asking of your tech.

We now know GTA 6 will be making the most of Tempest 3D Audio on PS5 and Dolby Atmos on Xbox, and while rumors swirl around the engine's reconstructive audio, this could well be the launchpad for an audio upgrade. The best gaming headsets will take full advantage of each console's spatial audio capabilities while adding extra features like simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth (for running your own soundtrack over Leonida), ANC, and fine-tuned EQ settings.

Whether you're leaving the TV speakers behind for the first time or retiring an aging, failing set of cups, it's worth remembering you don't need to jump to the top of the price range to find one of the best headsets for GTA 6.

We've been ears-on with the biggest releases from Razer, Logitech, SteelSeries, Turtle Beach, Corsair, and more over the six years of current-gen consoles. That means hunting down the best PS5 headsets and best Xbox Series X headsets on the daily, and finding the best value among them. You'll find all the best headsets we recommend for GTA 6 specifically just below.

Just to clear something up straight out the gate. The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless is no longer at the top of our top headset recommendation list. That's because the successor, the Nova Pro Omni, has secured the top spot with its Hi-Res audio. That full 96kHz response is only available on PC, though, which means GTA 6 players on consoles won't be getting their money's worth. The Pro Wireless still packs some of the best audio we've heard so far (and is fully Tempest-compatible) with hot-swappable batteries, ANC, and a quick-swap hub.

PS5 players can get away with a slightly lower price on the PlayStation model ($289.99 at Amazon), while Xbox players are looking at $299.99 at Amazon here.

The SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless is our top recommendation for those upgrading their gaming headset for GTA 6. You're getting the bold, spacious, punchy audio we've been celebrating for years here, with a particularly strong bass response for those engine revs, a super clear mid-range for that soundtrack, and a ton of space in the upper ranges for more directional awareness.

This is the audio we've been comparing the best PS5 headsets against for years, sitting alongside features we're yet to see replicated successfully across the market. ANC keeps the rest of the world firmly away from your Leonida adventures, while hot-swappable batteries mean you'll never need to charge up before jumping into the action.

Is the newer SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Omni our first shout in general? Yes, it boosts audio slightly - but mostly for PC players with its Hi-Res certification. It adds an extra USB port on the charging / EQ hub it carries over from the original, and improves the microphone clarity to boot. Considering it's often a whole $100 more than the Pro Wireless, and its main feature upgrade is locked behind a PC, though, the best headset for GTA 6 remains old faithful.

Just looking to upgrade from TV speakers ahead of GTA 6? The Turtle Beach Atlas 200 is our go-to budget headset for PS5. This wired connection keeps the price low but also removes the need for charging altogether. Don't let that lower price tag put you off the audio between these cups either. Times have moved on since the old days of cheap Turtle Beach headsets - we were impressed with the power and clarity of PS5 gameplay through these cans. As a fully licensed accessory, the Atlas 200 is also equipped for PlayStation's Tempest 3D engine as well.

If the Nova Pro Wireless is looking a little pricey, the Nova 5 Wireless is our next best recommendation from the brand behind some of the best audio we've heard on PS5. This is a cheaper alternative, dropping the fancy hot-swappable battery and central EQ hub system, but still keeping a high-quality audio profile. The Nova 5 also includes access to the Arctis app - a massive collection of over 300 per-game presets created by sound engineers and developers.

Don't want to spend the big bucks at the top of SteelSeries' range? There are plenty of cheaper alternatives that we still recommend every day. Turtle Beach even has an option readily found for less than $40 when the sales hit right.

What are you dropping from the experience? There are quality-of-life upgrades in the Nova Pro Wireless that you won't find further down the price scale. Hot-swappable batteries and active noise cancellation are two we've already looked at, but simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth connections can come in particularly handy if you're picking up calls or layering your own soundtrack over Leonida.

If you just want a set of great-sounding cups to accompany you on your next adventure without breaking the bank, though, we'd recommend the Turtle Beach Atlas 200 at the bottom of the price range and the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5 in the middle.

The Turtle Beach Stealth 500 is a little more expensive than PlayStation GTA 6 players' budget option, but it sports a wireless connection, powerful sound, and a lightweight design for those longer sessions. If you're already coming from a more premium set of cups, this won't be an upgrade. If you're investing in a setup that leaves those TV speakers behind for the first time, though, this is an excellent starting point for Xbox.

The SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5X is the same as the PlayStation model featured above, but adds compatibility for Microsoft's systems while also retaining the same PC and PS5 connection. You're getting the same powerful audio from a pedigree headset brand, with the same use of the Arctis app and its wealth of per-game presets.

Cheaper headsets are more difficult to come by on Xbox, but the overall best value budget option we've tested so far is the Turtle Beach Stealth 500. Just a little further up the price scale, you'll also find the Xbox version of the SteelSeries Arctis Nova 5.

That saved cash drops ANC, simultaneous 2.4GHz and Bluetooth connections, and hot-swappable batteries from the equation compared to the SteelSeries Arctis Nova Pro Wireless. Both still provide impressively powerful audio (with Dolby Atmos for Xbox) for their price, though, in a far more affordable package.

Kitting out a whole setup? We're also rounding up the best controllers for GTA 6 as well as the best PS5 accessories on the market.

#4056. "There’s always a night when Rome burns": South Of Midnight director says that Xbox funding it was "unsustainable", at least in hindsight

"I didn’t know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it"

Compulsion Games parted ways with former owners Xbox, having landed on the long list of things Microsoft were determined to ditch as part of multi-round mass cuts this year. Now, South of Midnight creative director David Sears has suggested that an eventual pulling of the rug was something he feared throughout the game's development, to the point where he seemingly doesn't think he'd have funded it if he'd been in the shoes of Xbox execs.

In an interview with MinnMax, Sears - who left Compulsion in March 2025 - outlined that ideally games big publishers put out aim to fall into one of two buckets. They either make lots of money or increase the prestige of the brand by becoming cultural touchstones across multiple generations. Obviously doing both is the perfect outcome, but Sears pegged South of Midnight as being more geared towards the latter camp. The likes of Double Fine's Keeper and Obsidian's Pentiment are other games which off the top of my head could be said to fit that same mold. The issue, of course, is that when push comes to shove, it's the games which can show a strong bottom line at any given moment which make the best case for their studios' short term survival if cash is tight.

So, South of Midnight lived in a risky place, with Sears recalling: "I literally told people. I was like, yeah, this could be terrible because somebody is going to say, one day, 'The money tap, we're closing those floodgates' and that's going to have really traumatic results downstream". The interviewer then asked Sears if what he was getting at is that, while he's glad Xbox funded South of Midnight, he might not have done so or at least cut the funding earlier if he was in charge of the console maker.

"Yeah, probably," Sears replied. "I mean, I wanted to make it. No doubt. Obviously, because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else's money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah, because I'm not completely selfless. It just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable. So, of course, it was going to have a 'shocking' outcome. I mean, it's easy to dissect it now, right? But at the time, I would talk to other directors and [they] would be like, 'How is this happening? I mean, how did we get so lucky? Is this a golden era?' And I would always be like, 'For now'. There's always a night when Rome burns and I didn't know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."

Notably, Sears added that in his view modern Microsoft showed a "more humane" side than the version of the company that existed in the 90s and early 2000s by giving studios like Compulsion a chance to spin out on their own rather than simply shuttering them outright once they were deemed surplus to requirements.

Given the director's no longer at Compulsion, it seems he'll not have a say on what their next game looks like, but as a newly indie studio one would imagine they'll have a keen eye on the bottom line.
